jobs.description:
**Hungry for a career that’s as rewarding as it is delicious?**

  

At Aspire Bakeries, we don’t just bake breads, cookies, and cakes - we create foods that bring people together. From La Brea Bakery® artisan breads to Otis Spunkmeyer® cookies, our products are enjoyed by millions of people every day. And behind every bite are talented manufacturing and support teams who take pride in their work and our food.

  

We’re looking for hard-working people who will bring integrity, creativity, and a passion for excellence to everything they do - whether that’s on the bakery floor, in the office, or supporting customers. In return, we offer a workplace culture built on care, ownership, and growth - where your contributions matter and your career can rise as high as our bread loaves!

  

With 13 commercial bakeries across North America and a reputation as an industry leader, Aspire Bakeries is rising together with our people and our customers to be the best all-around bakery solution. If you’re ready to grow with us, we’d love to hear from you.

  

**Why You’ll Love Working At Aspire Bakeries**  
  

* **Culture** - Our culture thrives on collaboration, diversity, and a shared passion for excellence. We support team members, empower growth, and encourage everyone to bring their authentic selves to work.
* **Health & Wellness** – Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus company-paid life insurance and additional voluntary options to fit your needs, including disability coverage.
* **Work-Life Balance** – Paid parental leave, generous paid time off, and holidays so you can recharge and spend time on what matters most.
* **Retirement Savings** – A competitive registered retirement plan (RPP) with immediate company match.
* **Growth & Development** – Opportunities to build skills, grow your career, and develop expertise through Aspire Bakeries’ learning and development programs.
* **Recognition & Rewards** – Performance incentive plans that celebrate achievements across sales, bakery performance, and individual contributions.

**About the Role**

We are seeking an **Engineering Co-op Student** (Fall term) to join our team at our **Brantford, ON bakery**. As an Engineering Co-op, you will support the Project Engineer in driving product development, manufacturing improvements, and facility upgrade initiatives that enhance operational efficiency and production capabilities.

  

**Shift & Schedule**

* Shift: Morning (Monday- Friday)
* Hours: 8 AM - 4:30 PM
* Weekend Availability: Required

**Compensation**

* Hourly Rate: $27

**Core Accountabilities (What You’ll be Doing)**

  

* Support engineering and manufacturing improvement projects to enhance production efficiency
* Develop and update plant layouts and technical drawings using AutoCAD
* Collaborate on equipment installations and new product start-ups within the facility
* Contribute to process optimization and line efficiency improvement initiatives
* Assist in project design, layout planning, and implementation activities
* Ensure compliance with GMP, food safety standards, and health & safety policies
* Maintain accurate documentation, SOP adherence, and support continuous improvement efforts
  

**Minimum Qualifications (What You Bring to the Table)**

  

* Currently enrolled in a post-secondary degree or diploma in Engineering or Engineering Technology
* Basic understanding of manufacturing processes and production environments
* Proficiency in AutoCAD
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, and Project
  

**Preferred Qualifications (Extra Ingredients for Success)**

  

* Experience in a food manufacturing or industrial environment
* Exposure to process improvement or lean manufacturing concepts
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Effective communication and teamwork abilities

We thank each applicant for taking the time and effort to submit an application; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. We do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to screen, assess, or select applicants

jobs.title: Engineering Intern - Aerostructures
jobs.description:
De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (DHC) is a storied name in the aerospace industry, recognized worldwide for its pioneering contributions to aviation and its unwavering commitment to quality, innovation, and reliability. Headquartered in Calgary, AB, DHC currently has approximately 2,400 employees across British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario, as well as in markets and distribution hubs world-wide.
  
  
Established in 1928, De Havilland Canada has a rich history marked by the development of some of the most iconic and versatile aircraft ever built. These aircraft have served a variety of roles—from bush flying to commercial aviation—and are celebrated for their rugged durability, operational versatility, and excellence in performance.
  
  
Over the decades, De Havilland Canada has evolved to meet the changing needs of the aviation industry. Today, we are more than just an aircraft manufacturer; we are a comprehensive aerospace company with capabilities that span design, production, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services. Our operations are supported by a team of skilled engineers, technicians, and industry professionals who are dedicated to upholding the highest standards of craftsmanship and innovation.
  
  
Role Profile
  
The Engineering Division is offering a 12 to 16-month internship opportunity in Aerostructure Engineering at our Calgary or Victoria location.
  
  
Please note, this internship will begin in January, 2027.
  
Strong preference for candidates who can work 12 to 16-months, open to candidates who can work for 8 months.
  
  
Role Overview
  
  
**The selected candidates will have the opportunity to:**  

* Provide support for Type Design Change projects as required.
* Draft and review drawing changes and DAO documents for type design changes under the direction of a design lead.
* Participate in integrated product development teams (IPDTs) as part of the engineering change notice (ECN) process.
* Modify, review, and create digital engineering data to support spares and production activities.
* Troubleshoot issues with digital definition.
* Assist in troubleshooting technical manufacturing issues and perform simple root cause analyses under the guidance of Methods Engineers.
* Create 2D/3D manufacturing data using , CATIA, SolidWorks and AutoCAD.
* Review existing engineering drawings and draft drawing changes to support design change projects.
* Support investigations and provide simple root cause analysis under supervision.
* Apply basic knowledge of stress analysis, material properties, and aerospace processing methods to support engineering change and manufacturing troubleshooting activities.

**What You'll Gain:**  

* Exposure to the full aircraft lifecycle—from design, test and delivery.
* Practical experience working on certification, production support, and fleet sustainment.
* Mentorship from senior engineers and insight into career paths across multiple disciplines.
* The chance to make real contributions to active engineering projects with national and international reach.

Education and Professional Qualifications
  

* Current engineering student (bachelor’s or masters)
* Preference to students who are completing an aerospace, Electrical or mechanical engineering degree

Additional Information
  

* Please submit your academic transcripts with your application.
* Relocation will not be provided
* Please note only those selected for an interview will be contacted

Why work at De Havilland?
  
De Havilland Canada is a Canadian-owned and operated aircraft manufacturer dedicated to providing rewarding opportunities in a diverse and welcoming workplace.
  

* Work with a team that makes a true difference in the world-making it possible for people to travel around the globe efficiently, comfortably and safely.
* We’ve manufactured over 5,600 aircraft including the most advanced turboprop in the air today. Our experience and expertise in constructing the highest performing aircraft in the industry is second to none.
* Our state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities are dynamic workplaces led by teams that support and encourage all employees.
* With a passionate team of innovators and a global network of support, De Havilland Canada proudly carries on it’s tradition as a leader in aerospace.

In addition to plenty of opportunities for career growth in a stimulating work environment, De Havilland Canada offers:
  

* Competitive wages
* Paid vacation
* Extended health benefits (medical, dental, vision, paramedical)
* Life insurance
* RRSP/DPSP Plan

As such, it is expected that all employees maintain strict adherence to Health & Safety Policies and to perform key physical tasks of the position described in the job description and interview process. This may include but is not limited to the ability to work in a variety of environmental conditions including temperature extremes, confined spaces, working at heights and with or around chemicals. Employees are expected to adhere to the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) when at work which must include but is not limited to the ability to maintain a positive fit test when mask use is required.

jobs.title: Engineering Co-op Student
jobs.description:
We’re looking for an Engineering Co-op Student to join our team, where you’ll get hands-on experience improving our engineering lab, building test setups, and supporting product development.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, learn how ideas are built and tested, and see the results of your work in the equipment our team uses.

Flexxaire is an Alberta-based manufacturer with products used globally. Our product lines include variable pitch fans (flexxaire.com) and automated coolant management systems (flexxcool.com).

**What you will work on**

Your initial focus will be improving our engineering lab and supporting the team’s testing capabilities. As projects progress, your interests and strengths will help shape opportunities in areas like:

* Lab Improvement: Help plan and implement a lab layout that supports safe, efficient testing, organize tools and components, and create storage, labelling, and documentation systems that are easy to maintain.
* Prototyping and Testing: Build, instrument, and troubleshoot test setups; develop repeatable procedures; and collect and analyze data for Flexxaire and FlexxCool development projects.
* Test Equipment and Installation: Assemble and improve test equipment, including upgrades to our FlexxCool test installation.
* Design and Fabrication: Take on projects involving CAD, component selection, purchasing, fabrication, and assembly, with guidance from the engineering team.
* Development Support: Document test results and equipment, help investigate problems, and support ongoing lab organization and equipment management.

**What is in it for you**

* Practical experience taking ideas from an initial concept to working equipment.
* Mentorship from engineers working across two product lines.
* Opportunities to build your skills in design, testing, and troubleshooting.
* A team that welcomes questions, encourages new ideas, and works together to solve problems.

**Who we are looking for**

You enjoy learning by doing, and bring curiosity, dependability, and attention to detail. Mechanical engineering is preferred, but we welcome students from other engineering disciplines with a strong practical interest. Experience with tools, CAD, or building and repairing things is an asset, whether gained through school, work, or personal projects.

**Job requirements**

**What we’re looking for**

* Practical mechanical aptitude and an interest in building, testing, and troubleshooting equipment.
* A willingness to get involved in hands-on lab and shop work.
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to keep work, equipment, and documentation organized.
* Initiative and dependable follow-through, with the judgement to ask questions when needed.
* A collaborative attitude, curiosity, and a commitment to working safely.

**Experience considered an asset**

* Building, repairing, or assembling things using hand and power tools.
* SolidWorks or similar CAD software.
* Test equipment, sensors, or collecting and analyzing data.

Experience gained through personal projects, student teams, coursework, or previous employment is equally welcome.

Job Type: Full-time

Benefits:

* On-site parking
* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

From your first day, you’ll be working on meaningful projects alongside experienced professionals. You’ll also take part in student-focused events, tours, and learning experiences that expand your knowledge and connect you with other students across the company.

You’ll engage with senior leaders and professionals for coaching, mentorship, and career development. Our division includes major players in the North American construction industry, including **Irving Equipment, Gulf Operators, CFM, Irving Wallboard, PumpsPlus,** and **Kent Homes.**

**This is more than just an internship.** It is a chance to contribute to real-world projects, build valuable skills, and grow your professional network.

* Mentorship & Job Shadowing - Connect with mentors and shadow professionals on job sites and in facilities to learn directly from the experts. We’re here to support your career growth.

We have exciting opportunities for engineering co-op students in our state-of-the-art sawmills in southern, and central NB and in Truro, NS.

  

Responsibilities may vary depending on site specific requirements. General responsibilities include:

* Coordinate projects by working alongside contractors and mill personnel to determine scope, planning, and execution of work packages for mill projects
* Lead specific projects with a team of sawmill staff and millwrights
* Work alongside senior management and site leaders to drive improvement throughout the site
* Champion safety, quality, and efficiency on the floor
* Learn the ins and outs of sawmill production and identify areas for improvement

  

* Engineering student in good academic standing, returning to school
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* High energy level with thorough attention to detail
* Self-motivated with a strong desire to improve operational processes
* Ability to effectively manage multiple assignments and shifting priorities
* Enjoy working in a team-oriented environment with Mill Staff, Unionized Trades People, Operators, Contractors and Suppliers to ensure projects are completed in a cost effective, timely, and safe manner
* Strong administrative abilities and computer skills (Microsoft Office)

  

**Irving Sawmills and Irving Forest Products** are committed to delivering quality lumber products, strong customer relationships and service reliability, as well as operating safe and efficient operations. We are focused on delivering quality products through continuous investment in our people, our forest products, our local communities and the most up-to-date technology.

Our employees work in some of the most technologically advanced facilities in North America. jobs.title: Co-op Student Mining Engineer
jobs.description:
**Are you someone passionate about reshaping the mining industry from early-stage planning to relinquishment and making a positive impact through mine planning work?**

If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you. We are growing and are on the lookout for an ambitious Student Mining Engineer to join our dynamic team for an 8–12-month co-op term. This placement is based in Okane’s Calgary office, so applicants must be willing to relocate to Calgary for the duration of the term. Come be a part of a visionary journey that is all about making a positive impact.

At Okane, we believe that integrated mine and closure planning is just the starting point to ‘Help Create a Better Tomorrow’. We work with mining companies to return land responsibly and safely, enabling what comes next to serve both people and the planet. Our work challenges the status quo — we advocate for meaningful partnerships with communities, including Indigenous rightsholders, and design solutions that create lasting financial, environmental, and social value. From early-stage planning through to relinquishment, we’re helping reshape the future of mining — and we’re looking for people who want to be part of that transformation.

Responsibilities:

In this role, you will work closely with our mining clients and technical teams on projects that span diverse sites with unique challenges to develop practical solutions for mine planning and closure.

**Your work will include:**

  

* In our fast-paced environment, your adaptability and prioritization skills will shine as you navigate unexpected challenges. As well as engaging in our critical thinking process, evaluating and recommending clever solutions in your work.

* You actively integrate health, safety and environmental considerations into every aspect of your work. This may look like completing hazard assessments and other HSE project requirements, following internal procedures and policies, participating in safety training, and promoting a safety culture.

* You’ll participate in background reviews that support the development of conceptual models. This is a great opportunity for you to learn about mine planning and get involved in creating detailed mine plans, material balances, and schedules that are essential for integrated life-of-mine and closure plans.

* You'll get to work closely with our experienced teams in geotechnical, geoscience, hydrology, and geochemistry.

* You’ll help design mine and tailings plans using engineering software.

* You’ll also have the chance to learn how to prepare cost estimates for projects and assist in writing technical documentation under the guidance of your mentors. This will be a fantastic learning experience as you contribute to proposals and technical reports that showcase our work.

* As you grow in your role, you’ll interact with both internal teams and external stakeholders, helping to build strong relationships.

* You’ll also assist in planning and conducting field investigations, such as material sampling programs, which will give you hands-on experience and a deeper understanding of mine planning operations.

Expectations for this Role:

* General understanding of mining process, lifecycle and mine closure concepts.

* Possess skills including communication, accountability, honesty, empathy, creativity, responsibility, and flexibility.

* Embody Okane’s Core Vision (Help Create a Better Tomorrow).

* You consistently model Okane Core Values (Passionate, Smart and Clever, Positive, Thoughtful and Caring, and Humble).

* You can adapt and prioritize navigating unexpected challenges.

* You actively engage in our critical thinking process, evaluating and recommending clever solutions in your work.

* You are comfortable working flexibly across time zones and travelling from time to time.

  
  

Qualifications:

* If you're currently enrolled in a undergraduate Mining Engineering or related engineering program and are eligible for a co-op work term.

* Familiarity with mine design and scheduling software such as Deswik CAD, Hexagon MinePlan, or RPM MinePlanner would be fantastic.

* Willingness and availability to travel to project sites as required, including occasional site rotations.

* Strong critical thinking skills to help you analyze information and evaluate various issues and risks.

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills are a must, as you'll interact with both internal and external stakeholders.

* Strong time management skills to help you manage tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Why Join Okane?

At Okane, we're committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, where every individual is valued for their unique contributions. Our dedicated teams span across the globe, connecting people from diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Our workplace culture is defined by the everyday behaviours of our team and driven by our Core Values: *Passionate, Thoughtful & Caring, Smart & Clever, Positive and Humble.* We believe in flexibility, work-life balance, and an open-door approach to communication.

  

We believe in personal and professional development, offering opportunities for continuous learning and growth. At Okane, we foster the opportunity for everyone to grow and develop their skills that align with their career path. As we continue to expand our global presence, we're looking for individuals who share our values and are dedicated to making a positive impact in the world.

How to Apply:

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact in the mining industry and contribute to sustainable land stewardship, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a cover letter detailing your experience, where you are studying and why you’re a great fit for this role before **November 20th, 2026.** Please note that only those candidates who are selected will be contacted.

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively in team environments.
* Willingness to participate in field assignments and site visits as required.
Demonstrated commitment to health, safety, quality, and continuous learning.

Why Choose WSP? We exist to shape communities to advance humanity. The brightest engineers, advisors and scientists from across the globe call WSP home.

• Proudly Canadian – we are a Top 100 Employer in Canada for 2026.
  
• A global community of brilliant minds – your next idea, mentor, or opportunity is always within reach.
  
• Limitless opportunities start here. Whether it's across the country or around the globe, we help you tailor your role to match your ambition — because your growth drives ours.
  
• Flexible work, real balance – we recognize the importance of balance in our lives and encourage you to prioritize the balance in yours.

#WeAreWSP

**AB, BC, NT, NU, SK & YT: $24.00 – $32.25**  
**MB & ON: $22.50 – $30.25**  
**NB, NL, NS, PEI & QC: $21.50 – $30.25**

The final salary awarded for this role may vary from the above range based on several factors including, but not limited to: relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs. These ranges may be subject to change for business purposes.

**Ready to Shape the Future?**

Your journey starts here. Join a team that is transforming how people and communities connect through world-class transit and rail infrastructure. Gain experience, build meaningful relationships, and contribute to projects that create lasting impact. Apply today and begin shaping the future of transportation with WSP.

  

At **WSP** , we exist to shape communities to advance humanity.
  
  
It’s why we bring people together who are wired to solve complex challenges—engineers, scientists, advisors, and technical experts who are driven by a common passion—to redefine what’s possible and shape what comes next. We are Visioneers.
  
  
As one of the world’s leading engineering, science and infrastructure solutions firms, we partner with clients across transportation, infrastructure, environment, buildings, energy, water, mining and metals. We pair deep local knowledge with global insights to pioneer solutions designed to leave a lasting, positive impact.
  
  
At **WSP** , you’ll join a community of brilliant minds that push boundaries every day - applying deep expertise and fuelling innovation to help create a more connected and resilient future. Here, your ideas are valued, your growth is supported, and you are encouraged to bring your authentic self to work. We empower our people to collaborate across disciplines, challenge the status quo, and shape a career with purpose.
  
  
Join us.

The PEY Analyst works within the Core Engineering team on projects on fundamental library development or on projects related to specific product development but can also be required to work on other business line initiatives as the priority changes in our dynamic trading environment.
  
  
Financial Engineering is a friendly and supportive group working within an exciting environment. Previous co-op students have moved on to various positions within the organization following graduation.

**Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:**  
  

* Assist the development and testing of cutting-edge derivatives pricing models
* Build quantitative tools for trading and structuring desks
* Build and maintain infrastructure processes for new business lines
* Ad hoc investigations for trading and marketing desks
* Conduct Mark-to-Market impact and sensitivity analysis for different models
* Provide support to the trading and sales desks

  
**Do you have the skills and requirements that will enable you to succeed in this role? – We’d love to work with you if:**
  
  

* You are currently enrolled in post-secondary education.
* You love to learn and envision yourself working for an international organization that heavily invests in your future.
* You enjoy being involved in extracurricular activities such as conferences, clubs, competitions, and/or hackathons.

* You have strong interpersonal skills, results oriented and a team player.
* You are able to work well in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
* You are currently enrolled in a Software Engineering, Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Business/Finance, Actuarial Science or other quantitative disciplines.

  
**What’s in it for you?**
  
  

* You’ll be part of a diverse, collaborative, innovative, and high-performing team.
* In-depth training to prepare you for the role, as well as ongoing coaching and feedback to help you succeed!
* Exclusive student events such as Scotia Student Day, Lunch & Learns, leadership panels, and much more!

jobs.description:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world!

  

We are looking for an ASIC Verification Intern to join our team working in the Toronto office!

In this position, you will handle the verification process of our groundbreaking memory subsystem components used in our Tegra SOCs using industry standard methodologies and practices. This position offers the opportunity to have a real impact on multiple product lines including consumer graphics, self-driving cars, HPC, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Understand the design, changes thoroughly and come up with comprehensive verification plans to verify them.
* Work with RTL engineers to help bring up features, debug failures and close coverage.
* Interact with the performance verification teams to augment verification through dynamic simulations and/or Formal verification techniques.
* Work with and enable FPGA and software teams to ensure that software is tested.
Be involved with post-silicon verification and debug.  

**What we need to see:**

* Pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or equivalent program area.
* Working knowledge computer architecture, logic design, verification, algorithms and data structures.
* Excellent debugging skills. Able to break problems down based on first principles.
* Working knowledge of PC systems, windows OS, and Linux.
* Possess good collaboration and cross-disciplinary teamwork skills.
Comfortable assuming different responsibilities over the life of a product.  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Verilog, SystemVerilog or UVM exposure.
* Familiar with scripting or programming languages such as C, C++, JAVA, Python, or Perl.
Background with memory controllers and/or DDR protocols.  

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. Are you creative and autonomous? Do you love a challenge? If so, we want to hear from you.

Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The expected hourly rate for this position is 29 CAD – 53 CAD.

You will also be eligible for Intern benefits .

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 23, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

AtkinsRéalis is one of Canada's largest private sector nuclear engineering groups. We have been providing a wide range of services to the nuclear industry in Canada and around the world since for more than 60 years. We are proud to be the steward of Canadian CANDU nuclear technology.

* Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

* Currently enrolled in Physics/Math/ Engineering Program with an accredited Canadian University.

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Be rewarded.

jobs.description:
Publication Date: Nov 7, 2026

Location:
St. Thomas, CA

Company: PowerCo Canada Inc.

Level of Experience: Intern

Job Function: Operations

Job ID: 4944

**Student-Factory Planning, AI & Simulation**
=============================================

**Who we are**

We are proud to announce the launch of Volkswagen Group’s largest cell factory, PowerCo, in St. Thomas. This is more than just a job – it’s a unique opportunity to shape the future of sustainable energy. Join us as we ramp up operations and help build a world-class company.

At PowerCo, we believe in fostering an environment where ambition meets collaboration, and where flexibility and creativity thrive. You'll be part of a diverse, talented team that is shaping the future of battery production. You’ll have the chance to advance your career while working alongside passionate colleagues who share a vision of making a lasting impact on the world.

Are you ready to be part of something exciting? Power up your career with us!

  

This is a 4-8 month temporary contract for a student attending a Canadian University. This is an in-person position located in St. Thomas.

  

**Your role and key responsibilities**

  

PowerCo Canada Inc. is building Volkswagen Group’s largest battery cell manufacturing facility in St. Thomas, Ontario, and is seeking a motivated Factory Planning, AI & Simulation Co-op to join its team. In this hands‑on developmental role, the selected candidate will contribute directly to the planning and optimization of a next‑generation battery production plant. The Co‑op student will support factory layout planning, BIM coordination, and simulation modeling to enable efficient, scalable, and future‑ready manufacturing operations. Responsibilities include developing 2D and 3D layouts, coordinating BIM models across engineering disciplines, and building simulation models for capacity and throughput analysis. This position provides exposure to advanced manufacturing planning, cross‑functional collaboration, and mentorship from experienced engineers. It represents an excellent opportunity for students seeking to apply strong analytical, technical, and organizational skills within a fast‑paced environment shaping the future of sustainable mobility.

The Co-op student will also support the identification, evaluation, and application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies to improve factory planning, simulation development, BIM coordination, and digital engineering workflows. The role will explore innovative approaches such as AI-assisted layout generation, simulation automation, data-driven decision support, and digital twin development to improve planning efficiency and manufacturing performance.

  

**What you bring to the team**

  

* Build high-level models using simulation software such as Siemens Plant Simulation and investigate AI-assisted model generation and validation approaches
* Run scenario analyses and leverage AI-assisted analytics to identify bottlenecks, optimization opportunities, and planning risks
* Collect and organize planning level data for capacity analysis
* Perform capacity and throughput calculations
* Support layout coordination and evaluate AI-enabled methods for 2D and 3D layout optimization, material flow analysis, and space utilization.
* Prepare summary reports, presentations and layout visual markups for project presentation and reviews
* Assist with quality control of 3D equipment models, placing equipment models within factory layout, and with clash management with tools such as Navisworks and Revit.
* Assist to keep models accurate and up-to-date, organize and maintain layout/BIM files and documentation.
* Deliver at least one proof-of-concept demonstrating how AI can improve factory planning efficiency, layout development, simulation creation, BIM coordination, capacity planning, or digital twin development.
* Quantify expected benefits and provide recommendations for future implementation within PowerCo planning processes.
* Research and evaluate AI applications for factory planning, BIM coordination, manufacturing simulation, and digital engineering.
* Identify opportunities to automate repetitive planning and modeling activities using AI tools.
* Support proof-of-concepts and pilot projects for AI-enabled planning solutions.
* Assess emerging technologies and recommend practical applications to improve planning efficiency and decision quality.

  

**What makes you stand out**

  

Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field in a Canadian institution. Preferably in a co-op program.

* Strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities.
* Interest in advanced manufacturing, industrial engineering, or production planning.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word)
* Basic understanding of technical drawings, process flows, or equipment layouts (AutoCAD/Revit/Navisworks/Siemens Plant Simulation exposure is a plus).
* Ability to work collaboratively in cross‑functional teams and communicate clearly.
* Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
* Willingness to learn new tools, processes, and documentation standards.
* Self‑driven, proactive, and comfortable working in a fast‑paced, evolving project environment.
* Strong interest in Artificial Intelligence, digital manufacturing, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
* Understanding of data analytics, automation, and machine learning concepts.
* Ability to evaluate emerging technologies and translate them into practical business applications.
* Strong analytical thinking and curiosity towards innovation and process improvement.
* Familiarity with simulation, CAD or 3D modeling tools is an asset
* Preferred experience in automotive or battery manufacturing
* Exposure to AI, machine learning, generative design, optimization algorithms, or digital twin concepts.
* Experience with Python, SQL, Power BI, Power Auto

**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

This is an existing vacancy.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

The Connectivity Business Group develops digital signal processing chips for leading-edge optical interfaces. The products designed by this group require You will be joining Marvell’s Interconnect architecture team, which develops advanced electrical and optical connectivity solutions for cloud, AI and data-center infrastructure. The team defines and evaluates system architectures that combine high-speed signaling, digital signal processing, error-correction coding, and system-level optimization to address the growing bandwidth, power, reliability, and performance requirements of next-generation interconnects. As an intern, you will develop models, analyze architectural tradeoffs, and design or optimize algorithms and system functions in collaboration with experienced architects and engineers. You will have the opportunity to translate research concepts into practical engineering solutions while contributing to technologies that form a critical part of the broader Marvell AI data-infrastructure portfolio.

**What You Can Expect**

* Develop system-level behavioral models for advanced optical interconnect architectures
* Design and implement DSP, error-correction coding, estimation or optimization algorithms for selected interconnect functions
* Analyze the effects of noise, system impairments and architectural parameters on performance
* Optimize selected system or DSP functions for performance, power, complexity, and robustness
* Validate modeling and simulation results using analytical methods, reference models, or available system data
* Collaborate with system architects and cross-functional engineering teams to review results and refine solutions
* Document and present technical progress, modeling results, and final outcomes

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a candidate who is currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028. Previous industry experience is not required.

* Research or project experience in digital signal processing, communication systems, system modeling, or a related field
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Knowledge of probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical signal processing or detection and estimation theory
* Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Python, Matlab, C or C++
* Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly in written and verbal form
* Ability to work effectively in a collaborative engineering environment

Additional preferred qualifications (any of these is a plus):

* Knowledge of error-correction coding, equalization, detection, or estimation algorithms
* Experience modeling noise, jitter, channel impairments, or other stochastic effects

Hitachi Rail provides signaling systems for metros and light rail systems. Our solutions provide efficient, safe, and green transportation solutions for people around the world.

  

As a Systems Design Intern, you will support the system engineering team for process and data collection and participate in design.

  

This safety critical industry provides challenging and rewarding work. The Systems Department is responsible to design the signaling solution based on the customer needs and the features provided by our product. The department is responsible for communicating this design to all stakeholders and ensuring that the design is understood and developed accordingly. The work environment is fast-paced and challenging as it involves working with customers, operators, and other suppliers to understand the full signaling solution and how the solution interacts with other systems in the transportation system. In addition, the design must meet all the safety, performance, functional and operational requirements. The team is also responsible for supporting the development and testing activities.

  

The incumbent is accountable for performing the design work correctly, within cost and schedule limits, as defined in approved work packages.

  

The work is typically defined by the Work Package Manager, then reviewed and approved by the Systems Architect and/or Manager. The System Engineer typically works with a team of engineers to define what will be designed, how it will perform and how it will be determined that it is working correctly.

* Importing contract requirements and other documents into IBM Rational DOORS

* Trace customer contract requirements to system level and/or lower-level requirements.

Accurately reports work progress and estimates to complete the assigned work.  

  

***SAFETY:***

Promotes a safety culture where product safety is paramount.  

  
  

**Key Requirements**

* The successful candidate should be working towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an accredited university or college in Systems, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or Computer Science, Mechatronics, or a related field.
* Completion of the second or third year of your undergraduate degree, or currently pursuing a master’s degree
* Good technical writing skills, excellent communication, and analytical skills; excellent command of the English language, both written and oral
* Familiarity with project work environment
* MS Office & Basic software and/or scripting knowledge
* The ability to work 40 hours a week in a hybrid environment for the duration of the internship is essential. **At least 2 days a week in the office.**

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

jobs.description:
**Who are we?**

We are CEM, a global data and insights firm for institutional investors including pension funds, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, family offices and sovereign wealth funds.

Our blue-chip corporate and government clients represent US$16 trillion in assets under management and over 100 million members. We provide them with objective insights to maximize value for money in both investments and pension administration. This helps our clients better understand where they stand and how to improve their performance. By improving our clients' performance, we, in turn, improve the financial well-being of pensioners globally.

How do we provide unique and actionable insight? By coupling the most extensive global database in the pension arena with unrivalled industry knowledge. All of this comes from experience - we have been at this since 1992. We were founded in Canada and expanded to the US and UK more than a decade ago.

We work together in a small company ambiance where your contributions will be appreciated, and your progress will be directly related to your ability and effort. Working at CEM, you will stretch your creative and analytical abilities while participating in the growth of a headline-making business.

**What are we looking for?**

We're looking for a Research Intern to join our Research & Analytics Team, where you'll build your skills through hands-on work on our custom research projects.

Working closely with experienced researchers, you'll do in-depth research and analysis, gather relevant data, spot industry trends, and present actionable insights that help our clients and partners succeed. Your work will draw on the most extensive global database in the pension field.

This internship is designed as a pathway to a full-time role. If the internship goes well, we intend to offer you a permanent position as a Research Analyst on our R&A Team.

**Internship Details**

* **Start date**: January 4, 2027
* **Duration**: 4 or 6 months
* **Location**: Hybrid, with 2 days a week in our Toronto office
* **Buddy program**: You'll be paired with a "buddy" from the Research Team to help you settle into our culture and our work.
* **Compensation**: Competitive
* **Pathway to full-time**: If you perform well, you can expect an offer to join CEM as a Research Analyst after the internship.

**What will you do in this role?**

* Contribute to two research projects commissioned by CEM client communities.
* Do in-depth research and analysis on topics relevant to institutional investors and pension funds.
* Gather, clean, and analyze data from our proprietary database and from external sources.
* Identify industry trends and turn your findings into clear, actionable insights.
* Prepare charts, summaries, and presentation materials for the R&A Team, clients, and partners.
* Present your findings to the Research Team and take part in team discussions.
* Raise questions and flag data issues early.

**What you’ll bring to this role?**

* A personal desire to make a difference in the financial well-being of pensioners.
* A university degree (completed or in progress) in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering or a related quantitative field.
* Some prior work experience is preferred, which may include internships, co-op placements, summer jobs, or up to 1 year of post-graduation experience.
* Strong analytical and research skills, and a curious mind that looks past surface-level data.
* The ability to find trends and build a narrative from large volumes of data.

The Stantec Internship Program provides students with valuable hands-on experience by working alongside experienced engineers, geoscientists, and technical specialists on projects in the mining, water-retaining infrastructure, and natural resource sectors. Through active involvement in project-related tasks and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, interns gain practical exposure to engineering consulting, develop technical and professional skills, and learn how academic concepts are applied in real-world projects.

The program also offers opportunities to build industry relationships, gain insight into project delivery and business operations, and develop a strong foundation for future career opportunities within Stantec.

Stantec’s Energy and Resources team delivers geotechnical solutions for mining, tailings, waste rock, dams, water storage, water conveyance, and hydropower projects. Our work supports projects from early site characterization and planning through analysis, design, construction, operation, and closure.

We have an exciting opportunity for a 2027 Geotechnical Engineering Co-op Student to join us for a term length that is flexible from 4 months to 18 month term commencing Summer 2027.

* Support engineers and geoscientists with mining geotechnical work for tailings storage facility, waste rock structure, open pit and other mining infrastructure.
* Assist with geotechnical calculations and analyses, which may include seepage, slope stability, settlement, liquefaction, deformation analysis, earthworks quantities, and material-property assessments under the guidance of experienced practitioners.

**Why SRC?**

With more than 400 employees, $83 million in annual revenue and nearly 80 years of RD&D experience, the Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC) is Canada’s second largest research and technology organization with 1,400 clients in 16 countries around the world. We help clients from across the world solve technology problems, make improvements, seize opportunities, maintain competitiveness, increase productivity, and develop new markets.

SRC is constructing North America’s first fully integrated, commercial demonstration Rare Earth Processing Facility with hydrometallurgy, separation and metal smelting stages. The facility is currently producing rare earth metals at commercial scale and is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2026. The Facility will be the first-of-its-kind in North America and will begin to establish a rare earth element (REE) technology hub in Saskatchewan, forming an industry model for future commercial REE initiatives and supply chain development.

**Overview**

SRC’s Rare Earth Element Division is seeking an Engineering Co-op Student to help support the construction, commissioning and operations for SRC’s Rare Earth Processing Facility. This position is a 16-month term, starting in May 2027.

**Accountabilities**

* Contribute to electrical and mechanical design deliverables for the Rare Earth Processing Facility
* Collaborate with the project team, including frequent communication and daily collaboration
* Assist senior engineers and designers with checking engineering deliverables, quality reviews and participating in construction and commissioning support activities including site visits, inspection, overseeing equipment testing, maintenance and installation

**Qualifications**

* A third or fourth year chemical, electrical or mechanical engineering student enrolled in the University of Saskatchewan Engineering Co-operative Internship Program

**Skills**

* Strong understanding of best practices for quality work and workplace safety
* Team player with effective interpersonal, communication, multitasking and problem-solving skills
* Willingness to learn and stay flexible as daily job tasks may vary
* Ability to self-motivate, follow detailed instructions and carry out tasks with minimal supervision
* Organizational skills and attention to detail

The chosen candidate will be required to provide an original Criminal Record Check that is satisfactory to SRC prior to the commencement of any employment duties. The Criminal Record Check must have been executed within the preceding 30 days of receipt.

This position is located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Deadline to apply is November 30, 2026.

Note: Applicants are also required to apply on Career Link as per the Co-op program requirements.

Please indicate on your application where you heard about the position as SRC works with several partners to support an inclusive workplace that embraces diverse backgrounds. Our goal is to engage and empower all people so they can successfully achieve their professional goals.

**As SRC strives to build a representative workforce, applications are encouraged from persons of Indigenous ancestry.**

**Hear from our Past Students**

As a working student, my internship experience at SRC has been incredibly valuable, providing me with hands-on exposure to real engineering projects and industry practices. One of the aspects I have enjoyed most is the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to meaningful work that has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. Throughout my placement, I have been able to apply concepts learned in my electrical engineering courses to real-world challenges while also gaining practical knowledge that cannot be learned in a classroom. This experience has increased my confidence as an engineer, and reinforced my enthusiasm for pursuing a career in engineering.

I'm currently a Chemical Engineering student and I've worked in both the Mineral Processing and Rare Earth Elements departments. My experience at SRC as a student assistant has been incredibly valuable, from working in bench scale lab projects and pilot plants to commissioning a brand new plant. While in school, it was hard to imagine what the processing equipment even looked like, all I knew was the math behind it. Now, I can say I've actually worked with the equipment including testing it, designing procedures for it, and troubling shooting it as well. Between both departments and others I've met throughout my time at SRC I can say for certain it is a warm and welcoming work environment. Overall, my Co-Op at SRC has been a great opportunity to grow, contribute, and gain experience that I’ll carry with me throughout my career.

**Operations NPI, Co-op**

Reference #43936

Waterdown, Ontario

**About L3HARRIS WESCAM**

As a subsidiary of L3Harris Technologies and within the Integrated Mission Systems Segment, the WESCAM division develops the most advanced optical sensor and targeting systems for global defense and military sectors, National Security, Search & Rescue and Airborne law enforcement agencies. From long-range covert surveillance missions to search and rescue operations, our MX-series systems, and the mission systems solutions they are a part of, produce stabilized high-magnification electro-optical and infrared images from airborne, marine and ground based platforms, enabling our customers to see first and act first.

**About the Role**

This is a 16 month co-op term with a role as an Operations Project Engineer focused on supporting New Product Introductions (NPI). Working under general direction and guidance and collaborating with contacts in Operations NPI Team to explain and interpret information. Contributes to the launch of new products and or variations of standard configurations into production to achieve operational targets that impact team results. Work consists of contribution to changes in processes to solve problems. Responsible for making minor changes in processes to solve problems or improve effectiveness of approaches being utilized. Expected to recommend solutions to problems for others review. Works to achieve operational targets within job area which has impact on the overall achievement of results for the team. Work is typically on smaller, less complex projects or task-related activities.

**Primary Responsibilities**

*Working in a cross-functional team with engineering, production, manufacturing engineering and procurement, this person is responsible for strategically identifying and tactically implementing improvements of WESCAM product, in accordance with product specifications and quality standards. This role is responsible for ensuring WESCAM’s product is serviceable and has robust processes through its lifecycle.*

* Lead and participate in assigned projects related to Operations activities
* Work in partnership with the project and cell teams to resolving technical issues and the development of new systems processes
* Support cell team activities and resolve issues on a daily basis
* Assist in the development of manufacturing processes and procedures for Production
* Capture and analyze data from Frontloading activities
* Reviewing change requests generated by engineering and mechanical staff, and implement changes as required
* Support any other business priorities as required by Operations leadership.

**Required Capabilities**

* Must have experience with a solid modelling CAD package, SolidWorks
* Familiar with Electro-Mechanical Manufacturing Processes
* Able to read and understand Mechanical drawings and Electrical schematics
* Experience and high interest in shop floor control activities
* Ability to manage multiple priorities within a Project-based environment
* Technical communication skills both verbal and written
* Must be well organized, goal oriented and able to give attention to detail
* Able to collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams across the organization
* Experience using SolidWorks, Composer and AutoCAD an asset, but not required

**Desired Education and Experiences**

* Enrollment in a Community College or University Mechanical, Mechatronics and or Electrical Engineering program

CIMCO is looking to hire a Automation Engineering Co-op student on a 12 or 16 month term starting January 2027. This position will be based out of our Burlington office.

Join our team! This is an existing vacancy that we are actively looking to fill.

**Role Responsibilities**

* Provide support in the design, configuration, integration, implementation and support of automation solutions for variety of systems in
* Recreation and Industrial refrigeration facilities. This includes the creation of DDC/PLC code and HMI interfaces based on company standards and specifications

jobs.title: Junior Mechanical CAD Designer - Co-op
jobs.description:
**About Delta Intelligent Building Technologies (Canada) Inc. (formerly known as Delta Controls).**

Delta Intelligent Building Technologies (Canada) Inc. (a subsidiary of Delta Electronics) is a leading building controls manufacturer with over 300 partners in more than 80 countries. For over three decades, we have provided innovative building automation solutions for commercial, healthcare, education, and leisure facilities. We delivered the world’s first fully integrated BACnet building solution for HVAC, lighting, and access control.

**Job Summary**

The Junior Mechanical CAD Designer is trained in Mechanical design and works with Senior Mechanical Designers and Electrical Hardware Designers to fix existing SolidWorks CAD files (3D & 2D) and upload them with the correct meta data to SolidWorks PDM.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The Junior Mechanical CAD Designer is expected to assist the Senior Mechanical Designers in:

* Checking existing SolidWorks CAD files
* Comparing the SolidWorks CAD files with the as built products
* Revising the SolidWorks CAD files if needed
* Fixing all SolidWorks CAD files and adding the missing meta data
* Upload the fixed SolidWorks CAD files to SolidWorks PDM
* Investigations into modelling
* Performing measurements to assist in completion of design checking
* Completing designs
* Maintenance of existing Mechanical designs and drawings
* Perform all work in accordance with established procedures and guidelines as described in the Product Development Process.

**Research and Design**

* Assist in research of new technology relevant to product directions.
* Assist in a technical analysis of proposed designs when requested.
* Assist in the generation of accurate Bill Of Materials for products and the different variations.
* Assist in the generation of conceptual 3D model designs
* Assist in the creation of detailed 3D model designs
* Generation of 2D control drawings

**Quality and Testing**

* Ensure all design and implementations are reviewed by the supervising senior hardware designers or QA hardware specialists.
* Assist in reviewing other mechanical designer’s work against requirements and quality standards.

**Documentation**

* Assist in the production of preliminary product documentation to communicate designs to other hardware designers, firmware developers, QA hardware specialists and manufacturing.

**Authority**

The Junior Mechanical CAD Designer has the authority to:

* Make and suggest changes or improvements to mechanical designs
* Suggest changes or improvements to QA Hardware Test procedures

**Key Attributes**

* Two years Technology Diploma in mechanical engineering (preferred)
* Strong understanding of mechanical design
* Experience with SolidWorks, SolidWorks PDM, technical drawings, plastic and sheet metal design…
* Experience with manufacturing processes
* Good interpersonal communication skills

**Work Location:** Hybrid (Currently 3 days a week, subject to change)  
**City:** Surrey  
**Type:** Co-op  
**Term**: Minimum 8 months, willing to go up to 1 year. Starting from January 2027  
**Salary:** $20-$26 per hour  
This range reflects the minimum and maximum target payable for the base salary of new hires across all Canadian locations. Actual compensation may vary outside this range and is dependent on various factors.

**Why work for us?**

We provide fantastic opportunities to individuals passionate about business and technology. Delta Electronics products are the most energy efficient power products in the industry, and our company is perfect for those who want to create, design and build sustainable solutions using massively scalable, big-data architecture, with a strong focus on building automation. Here are some of the Delta perks you’ll receive from day 1!

* Employee & safety centric culture with the possibility of remote work
* Flexible hours and scheduling available
* Competitive total compensation along with generous vacation allowances
* Three weeks of vacation
* In-house & external training provided along with education support and opportunities for growth
* Company funded annual personal development budget
* Financial benefits & planning such as group RRSP & company match
* Employer paid premiums for extended healthcare and family-focused benefits (health, vision and dental)
* Travel insurance coverage and access to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Wellness - onsite fitness center & company reimbursement for personal gym memberships
* Internal Recognition & Service Awards
* Employee Referral bonuses
* Transit accessible with free onsite parking
* Regular company events such as "Food Truck Fridays", Lunch & Learn and other planned activities

jobs.title: Mechanical Co-Op
jobs.description:
Cellula is looking to add a **Mechanical Co-op** to its Mechanical Engineering team to support its growing list of projects. This position will begin in **January** **2027**. We are open to both 4 or 8 month co-op terms, but with a preference for 8 months.

Cellula Robotics Ltd. is a world-leading marine technology company focused on changing the paradigm of subsea survey, science and security through modular, long range, autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) systems. Our company is growing and is transitioning from building mostly one-of-a-kind prototypes to completing the development of our four core products and will be delivering multiples of those products to our customers. Our products are configured for each client to deliver required capabilities to the end-user. We are committed to producing sustainable solutions for the defense, mineral exploration, and energy sectors driven by innovation and industry knowledge. We’re looking for enthusiastic and energetic people to join us in this growth and transition.

At Cellula we believe in collaboration, innovation, adaptability and reliability. These values are woven through all our products and how we do business. Our products are designed to be solutions to the challenges and capability needs of our clients, which often requires developing new capabilities and subsystems unique to a particular application. These systems are designed, built, and tested in-house by a skilled team of engineers, technicians, and support staff. People are at the heart of our business, and we pride ourselves in having a team-based workplace and building partnerships to solve the most difficult challenges in ocean technology. We believe in learning and innovating by doing. We send staff along with our products into the field to learn from our clients which informs our innovation.

As a company, we offer team members a chance to grow professionally with ever-changing projects. Our office is a casual, collaborative environment where you will be able to learn about our state-of-the-art systems from technical experts. In addition, we offer flexible work hours, benefits, and competitive compensation. This position is primarily an on-site position.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

* Create Concepts and develop detailed designs for both large and small-scale projects
* Generate and review drawings, calculations, and other documentation
* Prepare drawings, schematics, reports and proposals as required
* Prepare specifications for COTS components; find and evaluate suppliers
* Work with project team to ensure on-time project completion
* Assist in system assembly, integration, and troubleshooting
* Strive to ensure quality and timely delivery of finished products to clients

**Required Skills & Experience**

* Machine and mechanisms design
* Working knowledge of drive and actuation technologies
* 3D mechanical design
* Mechanical assembly skills
* Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
* Technical documentation: specifications, requirements, test plans/reports, operator manuals etc.
* Ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously
* Proven ability to meet deadlines/ successful completion of deliverables
* Analytical, thorough, resourceful and detail-oriented
* Team and customer service-focused
* Self-motivated, hardworking, flexible
* Thorough working knowledge of Solidworks software

**Desirable Skills & Experience**

* Experience in the subsea industry
* Robotic systems design experience
* Shop experience (forklift, scissor lift)
* Analytical skills - Matlab, Mathcad
* ISO9001 quality control

jobs.title: Engineering Co-op Student (Operations)
jobs.description:
**Why SRC?**

With more than 400 employees, $83 million in annual revenue and nearly 80 years of RD&D experience, the Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC) is Canada’s second largest research and technology organization with 1,400 clients in 16 countries around the world. We help clients from across the world solve technology problems, make improvements, seize opportunities, maintain competitiveness, increase productivity, and develop new markets.

SRC’s Rare Earth Processing Facility (REPF) is the first of its kind in Canada, laying the foundation for a REE supply chain in Saskatchewan and forming an industry model for future commercial REE resource expansion in the province. To learn more, visit www.src.sk.ca.

**Overview**

SRC’s Rare Earth Element Division is seeking an Engineering Co-op Student to help support the operations for SRC’s Rare Earth Processing Facility. This position is a 16-month term, starting in May 2027.

**Accountabilities**

* Assist the process engineering team with commissioning and start-up activities in the REPF
* Work with the operations and commissioning teams to diagnose upset or performance issues in the REPF
* Help develop the metallurgical accounting processes for the REPF
* Redline P&ID drawings for as-built conditions of the REPF
* Initiate Management of Change projects to improve safety, throughout, or quality in the REPF
* Build KPI dashboards and plant data reporting and visualization of REPF process data
* Spend a period of time on shift with the operators to better understand the day-to-day operation of the REPF

**Qualifications**

* A third or fourth year chemical, process, or computer engineering student enrolled in the University of Saskatchewan Engineering Co-operative Internship Program

**Skills**

* Strong understanding of best practices for quality work and workplace safety
* Team player with effective interpersonal, communication, multitasking and problem-solving skills
* Willingness to learn and stay flexible as daily job tasks may vary
* Ability to self-motivate, follow detailed instructions and carry out tasks with minimal supervision
* Organizational skills and attention to detail

The chosen candidate will be required to provide an original Criminal Record Check that is satisfactory to SRC prior to the commencement of any employment duties. The Criminal Record Check must have been executed within the preceding 30 days of receipt.

This position is located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Deadline to apply is November 30, 2026.

Note: Applicants are also required to apply on Career Link as per the Co-op program requirements.

Please indicate on your application where you heard about the position as SRC works with several partners to support an inclusive workplace that embraces diverse backgrounds. Our goal is to engage and empower all people so they can successfully achieve their professional goals.

**As SRC strives to build a representative workforce, applications are encouraged from persons of Indigenous ancestry.**

**Hear from our Past Students**

As a working student, my internship experience at SRC has been incredibly valuable, providing me with hands-on exposure to real engineering projects and industry practices. One of the aspects I have enjoyed most is the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to meaningful work that has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. Throughout my placement, I have been able to apply concepts learned in my electrical engineering courses to real-world challenges while also gaining practical knowledge that cannot be learned in a classroom. This experience has increased my confidence as an engineer, and reinforced my enthusiasm for pursuing a career in engineering.

* Mustafa Emara, Electrical Engineering Co-op Student

I'm currently a Chemical Engineering student and I've worked in both the Mineral Processing and Rare Earth Elements departments. My experience at SRC as a student assistant has been incredibly valuable, from working in bench scale lab projects and pilot plants to commissioning a brand new plant. While in school, it was hard to imagine what the processing equipment even looked like, all I knew was the math behind it. Now, I can say I've actually worked with the equipment including testing it, designing procedures for it, and troubling shooting it as well. Between both departments and others I've met throughout my time at SRC I can say for certain it is a warm and welcoming work environment. Overall, my Co-Op at SRC has been a great opportunity to grow, contribute, and gain experience that I’ll carry with me throughout my career.

* Mackenzie Wallace, Chemical Engineering Co-op Student

jobs.title: Compiler Engineering Graduate Intern
jobs.description:
**Job Details:**
================

**Job Description:**
--------------------

Join Us in Shaping the Future

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.

The Team
  
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.

Position Overview
  
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.

Responsibilities
  

* Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
* Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
* Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
* Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
* Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
* Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
* Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

  

**Success in This Role**

* Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.

* Clear written and verbal communication.

* Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.

* Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

* Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.

* Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.

* Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.

* Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.

* Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.

jobs.title: Engineering Co-op Field Student
jobs.description:
**Why SRC?**

With more than 400 employees, $83 million in annual revenue and nearly 80 years of RD&D experience, the Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC) is Canada’s second largest research and technology organization with 1,400 clients in 16 countries around the world. We help clients from across the world solve technology problems, make improvements, seize opportunities, maintain competitiveness, increase productivity, and develop new markets.

SRC’s Environmental Performance, Sustainability and Climate team provides environmental, technological, community engagement and management support services to the resource and industrial sectors. The team is managing a large-scale remediation project called Project CLEANS (Cleanup of Abandoned Northern Sites), which involves the remediation of 37 abandoned uranium mine and mill sites in northern Saskatchewan, with the objective of returning the sites to a state that supports safe, future use by the communities for traditional purposes. To learn more, visit www.src.sk.ca.

**Overview**

SRC’s Environmental Performance, Sustainability and Climate team is seeking an Engineering Co-op Student to engage in fieldwork activities in support of Project CLEANS. This position is a 16-month term, starting in May 2027.

**Accountabilities**

* Participate in fieldwork activities to support the assessment and remediation of abandoned uranium mines in northern Saskatchewan
* Conduct environmental sampling of soil, surface water, ground water and waste rock
* Perform radiation surveys and scanning
* Assist with environmental data management, analysis and interpretation
* Support the oversight of contractors during fieldwork
* Contribute to report preparation and the planning of field activities

**Qualifications**

* A third or fourth year environmental, geological or civil engineering student enrolled in the University of Saskatchewan Engineering Co-operative Internship Program
* Experience conducting field work is an asset

**Skills**

* Strong understanding of best practices for quality work and workplace safety
* Team player with effective interpersonal, communication, multitasking and problem-solving skills
* Willingness to learn and stay flexible as daily job tasks may vary
* Ability to self-motivate, follow detailed instructions and carry out tasks with minimal supervision
* Organizational skills and attention to detail

**Requirements**

* Valid Class 5 driver’s license
* Travel to remote, radiation-impacted abandoned mine sites in northern Saskatchewan for up to two weeks at a time during the field season (from May to October)
* Extended working hours (up to 12 hours per day) while in the field
* Out of town field trips for up to 21 days
* Traveling by small aircraft, boat and operating all-terrain vehicles
* Walking in rugged, forested terrain with 20-lb (10-kg) backpack for up to 10 hours per day
* Obtain designation as a Nuclear Energy Worker (training will be provided)

The chosen candidate will be required to provide an original Criminal Record Check that is satisfactory to SRC prior to the commencement of any employment duties. The Criminal Record Check must have been executed within the preceding 30 days of receipt.

This position is located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Deadline to apply is November 30, 2026.

Note: Applicants are also required to apply on Career Link as per the Co-op program requirements.

Please indicate on your application where you heard about the position as SRC works with several partners to support an inclusive workplace that embraces diverse backgrounds. Our goal is to engage and empower all people so they can successfully achieve their professional goals.

**As SRC strives to build a representative workforce, applications are encouraged from persons of Indigenous ancestry.**

**Hear from our Past Students**

As a working student, my internship experience at SRC has been incredibly valuable, providing me with hands-on exposure to real engineering projects and industry practices. One of the aspects I have enjoyed most is the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to meaningful work that has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. Throughout my placement, I have been able to apply concepts learned in my electrical engineering courses to real-world challenges while also gaining practical knowledge that cannot be learned in a classroom. This experience has increased my confidence as an engineer, and reinforced my enthusiasm for pursuing a career in engineering.

* Mustafa Emara, Electrical Engineering Co-op Student

I'm currently a Chemical Engineering student and I've worked in both the Mineral Processing and Rare Earth Elements departments. My experience at SRC as a student assistant has been incredibly valuable, from working in bench scale lab projects and pilot plants to commissioning a brand new plant. While in school, it was hard to imagine what the processing equipment even looked like, all I knew was the math behind it. Now, I can say I've actually worked with the equipment including testing it, designing procedures for it, and troubling shooting it as well. Between both departments and others I've met throughout my time at SRC I can say for certain it is a warm and welcoming work environment. Overall, my Co-Op at SRC has been a great opportunity to grow, contribute, and gain experience that I’ll carry with me throughout my career.

* Mackenzie Wallace, Chemical Engineering Co-op Student
