You’ll work alongside experienced engineers, learn how ideas are built and tested, and see the results of your work in the equipment our team uses.

Flexxaire is an Alberta-based manufacturer with products used globally. Our product lines include variable pitch fans (flexxaire.com) and automated coolant management systems (flexxcool.com).

**What you will work on**

Your initial focus will be improving our engineering lab and supporting the team’s testing capabilities. As projects progress, your interests and strengths will help shape opportunities in areas like:

* Lab Improvement: Help plan and implement a lab layout that supports safe, efficient testing, organize tools and components, and create storage, labelling, and documentation systems that are easy to maintain.
* Prototyping and Testing: Build, instrument, and troubleshoot test setups; develop repeatable procedures; and collect and analyze data for Flexxaire and FlexxCool development projects.
* Test Equipment and Installation: Assemble and improve test equipment, including upgrades to our FlexxCool test installation.
* Design and Fabrication: Take on projects involving CAD, component selection, purchasing, fabrication, and assembly, with guidance from the engineering team.
* Development Support: Document test results and equipment, help investigate problems, and support ongoing lab organization and equipment management.

**What is in it for you**

* Practical experience taking ideas from an initial concept to working equipment.
* Mentorship from engineers working across two product lines.
* Opportunities to build your skills in design, testing, and troubleshooting.
* A team that welcomes questions, encourages new ideas, and works together to solve problems.

**Who we are looking for**

You enjoy learning by doing, and bring curiosity, dependability, and attention to detail. Mechanical engineering is preferred, but we welcome students from other engineering disciplines with a strong practical interest. Experience with tools, CAD, or building and repairing things is an asset, whether gained through school, work, or personal projects.

* Practical mechanical aptitude and an interest in building, testing, and troubleshooting equipment.
* A willingness to get involved in hands-on lab and shop work.
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to keep work, equipment, and documentation organized.
* Initiative and dependable follow-through, with the judgement to ask questions when needed.
* A collaborative attitude, curiosity, and a commitment to working safely.

* Building, repairing, or assembling things using hand and power tools.

Experience gained through personal projects, student teams, coursework, or previous employment is equally welcome.

* On-site parking
* Paid time off

This placement is based in Okane’s Calgary office, so applicants must be willing to relocate to Calgary for the duration of the term. Come be a part of a visionary journey that is all about making a positive impact.

At Okane, we believe that integrated mine and closure planning is just the starting point to ‘Help Create a Better Tomorrow’. We work with mining companies to return land responsibly and safely, enabling what comes next to serve both people and the planet. Our work challenges the status quo — we advocate for meaningful partnerships with communities, including Indigenous rightsholders, and design solutions that create lasting financial, environmental, and social value. From early-stage planning through to relinquishment, we’re helping reshape the future of mining — and we’re looking for people who want to be part of that transformation.

Responsibilities:

In this role, you will work closely with our mining clients and technical teams on projects that span diverse sites with unique challenges to develop practical solutions for mine planning and closure.

**Your work will include:**

  

* In our fast-paced environment, your adaptability and prioritization skills will shine as you navigate unexpected challenges. As well as engaging in our critical thinking process, evaluating and recommending clever solutions in your work.

* You actively integrate health, safety and environmental considerations into every aspect of your work. This may look like completing hazard assessments and other HSE project requirements, following internal procedures and policies, participating in safety training, and promoting a safety culture.

* You’ll participate in background reviews that support the development of conceptual models. This is a great opportunity for you to learn about mine planning and get involved in creating detailed mine plans, material balances, and schedules that are essential for integrated life-of-mine and closure plans.

* You'll get to work closely with our experienced teams in geotechnical, geoscience, hydrology, and geochemistry.

* You’ll help design mine and tailings plans using engineering software.

* You’ll also have the chance to learn how to prepare cost estimates for projects and assist in writing technical documentation under the guidance of your mentors. This will be a fantastic learning experience as you contribute to proposals and technical reports that showcase our work.

* As you grow in your role, you’ll interact with both internal teams and external stakeholders, helping to build strong relationships.

* You’ll also assist in planning and conducting field investigations, such as material sampling programs, which will give you hands-on experience and a deeper understanding of mine planning operations.

Expectations for this Role:

* General understanding of mining process, lifecycle and mine closure concepts.

* Possess skills including communication, accountability, honesty, empathy, creativity, responsibility, and flexibility.

* Embody Okane’s Core Vision (Help Create a Better Tomorrow).

* You consistently model Okane Core Values (Passionate, Smart and Clever, Positive, Thoughtful and Caring, and Humble).

* You can adapt and prioritize navigating unexpected challenges.

* You actively engage in our critical thinking process, evaluating and recommending clever solutions in your work.

* You are comfortable working flexibly across time zones and travelling from time to time.

  
  

Qualifications:

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills are a must, as you'll interact with both internal and external stakeholders.

* Strong time management skills to help you manage tasks and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Why Join Okane?

At Okane, we're committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, where every individual is valued for their unique contributions. Our dedicated teams span across the globe, connecting people from diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

Our workplace culture is defined by the everyday behaviours of our team and driven by our Core Values: *Passionate, Thoughtful & Caring, Smart & Clever, Positive and Humble.* We believe in flexibility, work-life balance, and an open-door approach to communication.

  

We believe in personal and professional development, offering opportunities for continuous learning and growth. At Okane, we foster the opportunity for everyone to grow and develop their skills that align with their career path. As we continue to expand our global presence, we're looking for individuals who share our values and are dedicated to making a positive impact in the world.

As an Intern in Manufacturing Engineering here at Honeywell, you will gain hands-on experience and exposure to various aspects of our manufacturing operations. This role is designed to provide you with the opportunity to learn from industry professionals while contributing to meaningful projects that enhance our manufacturing processes and technologies.
  
  
You will report directly to our Manufacturing Engineering Manager, and you’ll work 100% on-site out of our North Vancouver, BC location.

The Internship will start in May 2027 and the minimum tenure is 4 months up to a year.

In this role, you will impact our manufacturing operations by assisting with process improvements, supporting engineering projects, and learning from experienced professionals in the field.

**KEY RESPONSABILITIES**

* Assist in the development and implementation of manufacturing processes and improvements.
* Support daily operations by providing technical assistance to the production team.
* Execute engineering design changes.
* Write manufacturing procedures, assisting in documentation and optimization, in the factory.
* Conduct research and analysis to aid in process optimization and efficiency enhancements.

  

**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Completed 2 years in a bachelor’s degree in engineering from an accredited institution.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
* Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
Familiarity with manufacturing processes or engineering principles.  

**WE VALUE**

* Electrical, mechatronics, software, mechanical or other industrial engineering related fields.
* Experience in a relevant field through coursework or previous internships.
* Experience in engineering software such as CAD and Labview.
* Previous internship experience in manufacturing engineering or a related field.
* Must be able to problem solve daily in a custom engineering and fabrication environment.
* Ability to work effectively in a team environment and communicate technical information clearly.

The hourly base range for this position is **$20/hr - $25/hr.** Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

**ABOUT HONEYWELL**

Honeywell International Inc. (Nasdaq: HON) invents and commercializes technologies that address some of the world’s most critical challenges around energy, safety, security, air travel, productivity, and global urbanization. We are a leading software-industrial company committed to introducing state-of-the-art technology solutions to improve efficiency, productivity, sustainability, and safety in high growth businesses in broad-based, attractive industrial end markets. Our products and solutions enable a safer, more comfortable, and more productive world, enhancing the quality of life of people around the globe. Learn more about Honeywell: **click here**

**THE BUSINESS UNIT**  
  
Honeywell Industrial Automation enables process industry operations, creates world-class sensor technologies, automates supply chains, makes warehouses smarter, and improves worker safety. This combination builds on our core strengths in controls and automation technologies which in turn allows us to deliver better commercial outcomes for our customers. We enable customers to enhance the safety, sustainability, resiliency, and productivity of their people, plants, and assets.

  
Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy.

**WELCOME TO VCNA!**

  

We are St Marys Cement, part of Votorantim Cimentos North America (VCNA).

Our commitment to excellence can be seen in those who invest and believe in what we do, those who share their lives with us, those who trust in our deliveries and those committed to innovation and a sustainable future.

  

Every day, we have the chance to accomplish something new and you're invited to be part of it.

  

**Summary/Job Scope:**

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented **Mechanical Engineering Co-op Student** to join our mechanical engineering team for an upcoming work term. This is an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment, working on real-world projects that contribute to our product development and operational efficiency.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Assist in the inspection, maintenance, and troubleshooting of mechanical equipment such as kilns, conveyors, crushers, and pumps.
* Assist in the design, development, and testing of mechanical components and systems.
* Support CAD modeling, drafting, and documentation using tools such as SolidWorks or AutoCAD.
* Conduct research and analysis to support engineering decisions.
* Support reliability engineering initiatives including vibration analysis, lubrication programs, and failure root cause analysis.
* Participate in mechanical design and drafting using CAD software (e.g., AutoCAD, SolidWorks).
* Help develop and update preventive maintenance procedures and documentation.
* Contribute to plant improvement projects focused on safety, efficiency, and sustainability.
* Collaborate with operations, electrical, and instrumentation teams to support cross-functional projects.
* Maintain accurate records of work performed and assist in preparing technical reports.
* Assist in the management of contractor/vendor services during plant shut down.
* Perform administrative tasks such as management of office supplies.
* Ensures the safety of themselves and all colleagues through enforcing safe work practices and providing motivation and effective communication.
  

**Note:** This job description may not cover all duties and requirements and may include additional tasks as assigned by the supervisor.

  

**Qualifications:**

* Enrolled in a Mechanical Engineering undergraduate program at a recognized Canadian institution.
* Completion of 1-2 years of study preferred.
* Strong understanding of mechanical systems and industrial equipment.
* Proficiency in CAD software and Microsoft Office Suite.
* Excellent organizational, problem-solving and communication skills.
* Ability to work in a physically demanding industrial environment.
* Ability to work well in a team and independently.
* Safety-conscious with a willingness to learn and follow plant protocols.
  

**Note**: This role is temporary for a maximum period of up to 1 year, with requirement where student must work at least 35 hours for a minimum of 12 weeks. The position is based out of Bowmanville, Ontario.

  

***Please note that the Bowmanville site is not easily accessible via public transit. Student will need to ensure transport to and from the plant in line with agreed schedule.***

  

**WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?**

Being part of VCNA is being part of building famous landmarks such as Toronto's CN Tower, Roy Thompson Hall, Maple Leaf Gardens and the Darlington Nuclear Station and Ryerson Centre, St. Regis Chicago and 150 N. Riverside, Louis High-Speed Rail in Chicago and more

* Opportunities to collaborate with teams around the globe and growth opportunities in different areas
* Training, professional development
* Access to Employees Resource Groups (ERGs), including SheBuilds, which fosters mentorship, leadership development and community support
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP): confidential support for you and your family (CAN)
* Flexible work environment with options for remote work
  

**Hourly Rate**: $25 per hour.

  

**OUR PEOPLE**

We care about people - all people. At VCNA, we take safety, health and wellness seriously. We're dedicated to giving our employees a safe workplace, our neighbors a safe environment and our customers a high-quality and safe product. Safety first -and always!

  

Our VC Way reflects who we are, inspiring us to unite our culture and be our best: Our Way of Being: ethical and respectful, Our Way of Working: together with excellence and Our Way of Thriving: with the courage to transform.

  

**INCLUSION AND EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYMENT**

We have a results-oriented culture that values being open, honest, and authentic. It's part of our DNA. We are continually expanding our diverse and inclusive team by providing opportunities for everyone, regardless of race, ethnicity, age, gender, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability or economic status - a workplace where you can express your individuality and be your best self!

**Electrical Engineering Co-op Student (Winter 2027)**
======================================================

  

**About Us**
------------

Ready to kickstart your career in one of Canada’s rapidly growing industries? Join Kinectrics, a company that takes pride in being consistently ranked as one of the best places to work in the nuclear and energy sector, where purpose and people mean as much as innovation and growth.

  

Since 2023, Kinectrics has employed over 200 students, providing them with the opportunity to grow and make a meaningful impact. Being recognized as Best Co-op Employer of the Year and recipient of the University of Waterloo Award for Next Generation Employment Innovation reflects our commitment to developing the next generation of talent.

  

**Shape Your Career With Kinectrics**
-------------------------------------

As a co-op student, you will:

* Have **priority consideration** for our Graduate Trainee program and full-time opportunities after graduation.
* Receive the tools and support you need to **grow professionally** with the opportunity to create impactful work that helps our clients achieve their goals.
* Gain **practical work experience to complement your classroom studies** and experience what it is really like to work in the industry, while working with technical experts to hone your skills.
* Build rapport and **make vital connections with industry experts** through networking and mentorship during your work term.
* Join a **large community of co-op students** from different schools and backgrounds.

Your journey at Kinectrics does not have to end there! Many students return for additional co-op terms or transition into full-time roles.

  

**About the Position**

* **Department:** High Voltage Safety Testing (HVST)
* **Location:** 800 Kipling Avenue, Toronto, ON - On-site
* **Term Length:** 12 or 16 months

* High level of initiative.

  + Database development, i.e. Oracle, Microsoft Access.

At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

  
  

We are seeking a motivated Engineering Intern to support the Quality department for our ReliaGear product line. This role will focus on documentation control and continuous improvement initiatives, contributing to the reliability, compliance, and efficiency of our quality processes.

  
  

This internship provides hands-on exposure to a dynamic manufacturing environment and offers the opportunity to work on impactful projects aligned with operational excellence. This is an in person internship.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Review, update, and standardize quality documentation (work instructions, procedures, test reports)
* Ensure document compliance with internal standards and regulatory requirements
* Support implementation and maintenance of document control systems
* Track revisions and manage version control to ensure accuracy and traceability
* Contribute to ongoing continuous improvement initiatives within the ReliaGear line
* Analyze quality data to identify improvement opportunities
* Support root cause analysis and corrective actions (e.g., using tools like 5 Whys, Fishbone diagrams)
* Participate in process optimization and efficiency improvement efforts
* Assist in developing and documenting new best practices
* Assist in executing or documenting testing procedures

St. Thomas, CA

**Student-Factory Planning, AI & Simulation**
=============================================

**Who we are**

We are proud to announce the launch of Volkswagen Group’s largest cell factory, PowerCo, in St. Thomas. This is more than just a job – it’s a unique opportunity to shape the future of sustainable energy. Join us as we ramp up operations and help build a world-class company.

At PowerCo, we believe in fostering an environment where ambition meets collaboration, and where flexibility and creativity thrive. You'll be part of a diverse, talented team that is shaping the future of battery production. You’ll have the chance to advance your career while working alongside passionate colleagues who share a vision of making a lasting impact on the world.

Are you ready to be part of something exciting? Power up your career with us!

  

This is a 4-8 month temporary contract for a student attending a Canadian University. This is an in-person position located in St. Thomas.

  

**Your role and key responsibilities**

  

PowerCo Canada Inc. is building Volkswagen Group’s largest battery cell manufacturing facility in St. Thomas, Ontario, and is seeking a motivated Factory Planning, AI & Simulation Co-op to join its team. In this hands‑on developmental role, the selected candidate will contribute directly to the planning and optimization of a next‑generation battery production plant. The Co‑op student will support factory layout planning, BIM coordination, and simulation modeling to enable efficient, scalable, and future‑ready manufacturing operations. Responsibilities include developing 2D and 3D layouts, coordinating BIM models across engineering disciplines, and building simulation models for capacity and throughput analysis. This position provides exposure to advanced manufacturing planning, cross‑functional collaboration, and mentorship from experienced engineers. It represents an excellent opportunity for students seeking to apply strong analytical, technical, and organizational skills within a fast‑paced environment shaping the future of sustainable mobility.

The Co-op student will also support the identification, evaluation, and application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies to improve factory planning, simulation development, BIM coordination, and digital engineering workflows. The role will explore innovative approaches such as AI-assisted layout generation, simulation automation, data-driven decision support, and digital twin development to improve planning efficiency and manufacturing performance.

  

**What you bring to the team**

  

* Build high-level models using simulation software such as Siemens Plant Simulation and investigate AI-assisted model generation and validation approaches
* Run scenario analyses and leverage AI-assisted analytics to identify bottlenecks, optimization opportunities, and planning risks
* Collect and organize planning level data for capacity analysis
* Perform capacity and throughput calculations
* Support layout coordination and evaluate AI-enabled methods for 2D and 3D layout optimization, material flow analysis, and space utilization.
* Prepare summary reports, presentations and layout visual markups for project presentation and reviews
* Assist with quality control of 3D equipment models, placing equipment models within factory layout, and with clash management with tools such as Navisworks and Revit.
* Assist to keep models accurate and up-to-date, organize and maintain layout/BIM files and documentation.
* Deliver at least one proof-of-concept demonstrating how AI can improve factory planning efficiency, layout development, simulation creation, BIM coordination, capacity planning, or digital twin development.
* Quantify expected benefits and provide recommendations for future implementation within PowerCo planning processes.
* Research and evaluate AI applications for factory planning, BIM coordination, manufacturing simulation, and digital engineering.
* Identify opportunities to automate repetitive planning and modeling activities using AI tools.
* Support proof-of-concepts and pilot projects for AI-enabled planning solutions.
* Assess emerging technologies and recommend practical applications to improve planning efficiency and decision quality.

  

**What makes you stand out**

  

Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field in a Canadian institution. Preferably in a co-op program.

* Strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities.
* Interest in advanced manufacturing, industrial engineering, or production planning.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word)
* Basic understanding of technical drawings, process flows, or equipment layouts (AutoCAD/Revit/Navisworks/Siemens Plant Simulation exposure is a plus).
* Ability to work collaboratively in cross‑functional teams and communicate clearly.
* Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
* Willingness to learn new tools, processes, and documentation standards.
* Self‑driven, proactive, and comfortable working in a fast‑paced, evolving project environment.
* Strong interest in Artificial Intelligence, digital manufacturing, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
* Understanding of data analytics, automation, and machine learning concepts.
* Ability to evaluate emerging technologies and translate them into practical business applications.
* Strong analytical thinking and curiosity towards innovation and process improvement.
* Familiarity with simulation, CAD or 3D modeling tools is an asset
* Preferred experience in automotive or battery manufacturing
* Exposure to AI, machine learning, generative design, optimization algorithms, or digital twin concepts.
* Experience with Python, SQL, Power BI, Power Auto

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

This is an existing vacancy.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

The Connectivity Business Group develops digital signal processing chips for leading-edge optical interfaces. The products designed by this group require You will be joining Marvell’s Interconnect architecture team, which develops advanced electrical and optical connectivity solutions for cloud, AI and data-center infrastructure. The team defines and evaluates system architectures that combine high-speed signaling, digital signal processing, error-correction coding, and system-level optimization to address the growing bandwidth, power, reliability, and performance requirements of next-generation interconnects. As an intern, you will develop models, analyze architectural tradeoffs, and design or optimize algorithms and system functions in collaboration with experienced architects and engineers. You will have the opportunity to translate research concepts into practical engineering solutions while contributing to technologies that form a critical part of the broader Marvell AI data-infrastructure portfolio.

**What You Can Expect**

* Develop system-level behavioral models for advanced optical interconnect architectures
* Design and implement DSP, error-correction coding, estimation or optimization algorithms for selected interconnect functions
* Analyze the effects of noise, system impairments and architectural parameters on performance
* Optimize selected system or DSP functions for performance, power, complexity, and robustness
* Validate modeling and simulation results using analytical methods, reference models, or available system data
* Collaborate with system architects and cross-functional engineering teams to review results and refine solutions
* Document and present technical progress, modeling results, and final outcomes

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a candidate who is currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field, with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028. Previous industry experience is not required.

Minimum qualifications:

* Research or project experience in digital signal processing, communication systems, system modeling, or a related field
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Knowledge of probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical signal processing or detection and estimation theory
* Proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Python, Matlab, C or C++
* Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly in written and verbal form
* Ability to work effectively in a collaborative engineering environment

Additional preferred qualifications (any of these is a plus):

* Knowledge of error-correction coding, equalization, detection, or estimation algorithms
* Experience modeling noise, jitter, channel impairments, or other stochastic effects
* Experience with theory and practice of optimization algorithms· Familiarity with photonics or optoelectronic systems
* Familiarity with high-speed electrical or optical interconnect systems
* Experience with hardware-oriented modeling and implementation considerations

**Expected Base Pay Range (CAD)**

36 - 48, $ per hour.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

With competitive compensation and great benefits, you will enjoy our workstyle within an environment of shared collaboration, transparency, and inclusivity. We’re dedicated to giving our people the tools and resources they need to succeed in doing work that matters, and to grow and develop with us. For additional information on what it’s like to work at Marvell, visit our Careers page.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

**This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.**

**Who are we?**

We are CEM, a global data and insights firm for institutional investors including pension funds, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, family offices and sovereign wealth funds.

Our blue-chip corporate and government clients represent US$16 trillion in assets under management and over 100 million members. We provide them with objective insights to maximize value for money in both investments and pension administration. This helps our clients better understand where they stand and how to improve their performance. By improving our clients' performance, we, in turn, improve the financial well-being of pensioners globally.

How do we provide unique and actionable insight? By coupling the most extensive global database in the pension arena with unrivalled industry knowledge. All of this comes from experience - we have been at this since 1992. We were founded in Canada and expanded to the US and UK more than a decade ago.

We work together in a small company ambiance where your contributions will be appreciated, and your progress will be directly related to your ability and effort. Working at CEM, you will stretch your creative and analytical abilities while participating in the growth of a headline-making business.

**What are we looking for?**

We're looking for a Research Intern to join our Research & Analytics Team, where you'll build your skills through hands-on work on our custom research projects.

Working closely with experienced researchers, you'll do in-depth research and analysis, gather relevant data, spot industry trends, and present actionable insights that help our clients and partners succeed. Your work will draw on the most extensive global database in the pension field.

This internship is designed as a pathway to a full-time role. If the internship goes well, we intend to offer you a permanent position as a Research Analyst on our R&A Team.

**Internship Details**

* **Start date**: January 4, 2027
* **Duration**: 4 or 6 months
* **Location**: Hybrid, with 2 days a week in our Toronto office
* **Buddy program**: You'll be paired with a "buddy" from the Research Team to help you settle into our culture and our work.
* **Compensation**: Competitive
* **Pathway to full-time**: If you perform well, you can expect an offer to join CEM as a Research Analyst after the internship.

**What will you do in this role?**

* Contribute to two research projects commissioned by CEM client communities.
* Do in-depth research and analysis on topics relevant to institutional investors and pension funds.
* Gather, clean, and analyze data from our proprietary database and from external sources.
* Identify industry trends and turn your findings into clear, actionable insights.
* Prepare charts, summaries, and presentation materials for the R&A Team, clients, and partners.
* Present your findings to the Research Team and take part in team discussions.
* Raise questions and flag data issues early.

**What you’ll bring to this role?**

* A personal desire to make a difference in the financial well-being of pensioners.
* A university degree (completed or in progress) in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering or a related quantitative field.
* Some prior work experience is preferred, which may include internships, co-op placements, summer jobs, or up to 1 year of post-graduation experience.
* Strong analytical and research skills, and a curious mind that looks past surface-level data.
* The ability to find trends and build a narrative from large volumes of data.
* Strong Excel skills. Experience with Python, R, or SQL is an asset.
* Excellent writing and communication skills.
* An interest in investments, pensions or capital markets. Previous internship or co-op experience in the field is an asset.
* Fluency in written and spoken French and Dutch is an asset; proficiency in other languages is also considered an advantage.

**What does success look like in this role?**

* Deliver consistently accurate work with minimal rework
* Contribute meaningfully to high-quality research.
* Turn complex data into clear, compelling insights.
* Build strong, collaborative relationships with the R&A Team.
* Show the curiosity, ownership, and growth that set you up to transition into a full-time Research Analyst role.

**Why join us?**

* Work directly with some of Canada's leading pension funds and institutional investors.
* Publish research that shapes thinking across the global pension industry.
* Enjoy the agility of a growing firm with the stability of an established global organization.
* Work with a highly collaborative team where your ideas shape business decisions.
* Opportunities to work with complex datasets to draw elegant insights.
* A hybrid work environment, 2 days a week in the office.
* A curiosity-driven culture founded on a desire to improve lives.
* A team that is stronger for its gender, cultural, and intellectual diversity.

**Ready to make an impact?**

If you love digging into data, enjoy turning research into stories, and want to grow your career while helping improve the financial well-being of pensioners, we'd love to hear from you!

The Stantec Internship Program provides students with valuable hands-on experience by working alongside experienced engineers, geoscientists, and technical specialists on projects in the mining, water-retaining infrastructure, and natural resource sectors. Through active involvement in project-related tasks and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, interns gain practical exposure to engineering consulting, develop technical and professional skills, and learn how academic concepts are applied in real-world projects.

The program also offers opportunities to build industry relationships, gain insight into project delivery and business operations, and develop a strong foundation for future career opportunities within Stantec.

Stantec’s Energy and Resources team delivers geotechnical solutions for mining, tailings, waste rock, dams, water storage, water conveyance, and hydropower projects. Our work supports projects from early site characterization and planning through analysis, design, construction, operation, and closure.

We have an exciting opportunity for a 2027 Geotechnical Engineering Co-op Student to join us for a term length that is flexible from 4 months to 18 month term commencing Summer 2027.

**Why SRC?**

With more than 400 employees, $83 million in annual revenue and nearly 80 years of RD&D experience, the Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC) is Canada’s second largest research and technology organization with 1,400 clients in 16 countries around the world. We help clients from across the world solve technology problems, make improvements, seize opportunities, maintain competitiveness, increase productivity, and develop new markets.

SRC is constructing North America’s first fully integrated, commercial demonstration Rare Earth Processing Facility with hydrometallurgy, separation and metal smelting stages. The facility is currently producing rare earth metals at commercial scale and is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2026. The Facility will be the first-of-its-kind in North America and will begin to establish a rare earth element (REE) technology hub in Saskatchewan, forming an industry model for future commercial REE initiatives and supply chain development.

**Overview**

SRC’s Rare Earth Element Division is seeking an Engineering Co-op Student to help support the construction, commissioning and operations for SRC’s Rare Earth Processing Facility. This position is a 16-month term, starting in May 2027.

**Accountabilities**

* Contribute to electrical and mechanical design deliverables for the Rare Earth Processing Facility
* Collaborate with the project team, including frequent communication and daily collaboration
* Assist senior engineers and designers with checking engineering deliverables, quality reviews and participating in construction and commissioning support activities including site visits, inspection, overseeing equipment testing, maintenance and installation

**Qualifications**

* A third or fourth year chemical, electrical or mechanical engineering student enrolled in the University of Saskatchewan Engineering Co-operative Internship Program

**Skills**

* Strong understanding of best practices for quality work and workplace safety
* Team player with effective interpersonal, communication, multitasking and problem-solving skills
* Willingness to learn and stay flexible as daily job tasks may vary
* Ability to self-motivate, follow detailed instructions and carry out tasks with minimal supervision
* Organizational skills and attention to detail

The chosen candidate will be required to provide an original Criminal Record Check that is satisfactory to SRC prior to the commencement of any employment duties. The Criminal Record Check must have been executed within the preceding 30 days of receipt.

This position is located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Deadline to apply is November 30, 2026.

Note: Applicants are also required to apply on Career Link as per the Co-op program requirements.

Please indicate on your application where you heard about the position as SRC works with several partners to support an inclusive workplace that embraces diverse backgrounds. Our goal is to engage and empower all people so they can successfully achieve their professional goals.

**As SRC strives to build a representative workforce, applications are encouraged from persons of Indigenous ancestry.**

**Hear from our Past Students**

As a working student, my internship experience at SRC has been incredibly valuable, providing me with hands-on exposure to real engineering projects and industry practices. One of the aspects I have enjoyed most is the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to meaningful work that has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. Throughout my placement, I have been able to apply concepts learned in my electrical engineering courses to real-world challenges while also gaining practical knowledge that cannot be learned in a classroom. This experience has increased my confidence as an engineer, and reinforced my enthusiasm for pursuing a career in engineering.

* Mustafa Emara, Electrical Engineering Co-op Student

I'm currently a Chemical Engineering student and I've worked in both the Mineral Processing and Rare Earth Elements departments. My experience at SRC as a student assistant has been incredibly valuable, from working in bench scale lab projects and pilot plants to commissioning a brand new plant. While in school, it was hard to imagine what the processing equipment even looked like, all I knew was the math behind it. Now, I can say I've actually worked with the equipment including testing it, designing procedures for it, and troubling shooting it as well. Between both departments and others I've met throughout my time at SRC I can say for certain it is a warm and welcoming work environment. Overall, my Co-Op at SRC has been a great opportunity to grow, contribute, and gain experience that I’ll carry with me throughout my career.

* Mackenzie Wallace, Chemical Engineering Co-op Student

new_jobs.description:
**Electrical Design and Embedded Software Engineering Intern**
==============================================================

Boucherville, Quebec, CA, Canada

Requisition: 68493

**Job Purpose**
---------------

Dana is a global leader in the supply of highly engineered driveline, sealing, and thermal-management technologies that improve the efficiency and performance of vehicles with both conventional and alternative-energy powertrains.

  

Serving three primary markets – passenger vehicle, commercial truck, and the off-highway equipment – Dana provides the world’s original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket with local product and service support through a network of nearly 100 engineering, manufacturing, and distribution facilities.

  

Power up your career and become part of our driving force! Join us in developing and advancing clean, efficient, and high-performance technologies, and contribute to the growth of transportation electrification.

  

Our Embedded Software team requires a compact Hardware-in-the-Loop (mini-HIL) test bench to test inverter control software without a motor, power stage, or high-voltage installation. The mini-HIL is a custom electronic board (PCBA) that connects to the inverter control board. It emulates the power stage and motor by generating realistic sensor signals.

**Job Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------

Help revolutionize the transportation industry while:

* Analyzing existing mini-HIL schematics, PCB layouts, and documentation, then bringing up and debugging the current prototype.
* Designing signal emulation circuits, including DAC stages and operational amplifiers for current and voltage sensor emulation, thermistor emulation, resolver emulation synchronized with the excitation signal, as well as fault injection and signal override capabilities.
* Designing acquisition circuits for PWM outputs, gate-drive commands, and digital outputs from the product board, including level shifting and input protection.
* Performing component placement and PCBA routing.
* Bringing up and validating the new board using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, signal generators, and multimeters.
* Developing the board’s embedded firmware.
* Developing scripts and tools (e.g., in Python) to configure, control, and automate testing on the mini-HIL bench.
* Documenting your work, including design notes, schematics, user guides, and test reports.
* Performing any other related duties as required..

**Education and Qualifications**
--------------------------------

Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field;

**Skills**
----------

* Experience with schematic capture and PCB design tools (Altium Designer, KiCad, or equivalent), gained through academic projects, previous internships, or personal projects.
* Knowledge of analog and mixed-signal circuit design, including operational amplifiers, filtering, ADC/DAC, signal conditioning, and signal protection.
* Programming experience in C, C++, and Python.
* Experience with software development tools (Git, Azure DevOps, JIRA, etc.).
* Experience with 32-bit microcontrollers (Infineon, TI, ARM, etc.) and JTAG debugging tools.
* A proactive mindset and strong ability to work independently.
* The ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
* Demonstrated ability to thoroughly document work and technical deliverables.
* Proficiency in both French and English, spoken and written.

Join our team of 28,000 problem solvers who are fostering a culture of innovation by leveraging the diverse perspectives of our global team. We believe in facing challenges head-on by finding opportunity and uncovering possibility, where roadblocks and barriers become targets instead of obstacles. We are One Dana with limitless opportunity.

#### **Our Values**

* Value Others
* Inspire Innovation
* Grow Responsibly
* Win Together

**Who we are**

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

**About Samsara Hardware Engineering:**

Samsara's hardware systems bridge the gap between the rapidly evolving world of physical operations and our cloud platform that enables our customers to increase the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of their operations which power the global economy. The hardware footprint is big – we build ultra-low power sensors, ruggedized asset trackers, vehicle ADAS systems with AI/ML, telematics systems, and rackmount video inspection with AI/Ml, with more to come in the future. We leverage myriad technologies including low-power MCUs, big SoCs, DSPs, LTE, GPS, BLE, WiFi, imaging sensors, ML/AI/CV, accelerometers, and more. Our challenges span the gamut from eeking out single-digit microamps to thermals to desense to cost reduction to antenna design to enclosure design that survives extreme environments.

**About the role:**

We're looking for an Electrical Engineer co-op to join our team. In the day-to-day, you will be responsible for working on the EE aspects of the design of products based on thorough feasibility, design, and cost studies encompassing key component selection, thermals, antenna, etc. We have a tremendous amount of telemetry and access to customers that help guide our design process. We run a collaborative process working closely with Product Management, PD, FW, EPM, NPI, and Hardware leadership to make excellent tradeoffs and choices. The US and Taiwan EE teams are supported by the Supply Chain team, laboratories, JDM design resources, and a growing supply base. You will work closely with these internal and external partners to achieve our objectives.

Ideally, this student is in their junior year of school as an undergraduate student and has previous internship and/or co-op experience.**

We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, and countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
* **You're energized by our opportunity:** The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
* **You want to be with the best:** At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.

**In this role, you will:**

* Contribute to shipping successful product lines.

* Know the system: Evaluate system feature tradeoffs and create the system specifications for development with product management and cross-functional engineering teams.
* Prototype: Assemble EVKs, board hacks, or quick-turn fabrication for evaluating concepts or jump-starting firmware development.
* Design: Take a concept from block diagram to schematics and through layout; either on your own or navigate the process with JDM resources.
* Test: Create a validation plan for each phase of the product development through PVT and characterize the full electrical system for function, power, and use-cases.
* Failure analysis: Find the root cause of design inefficiencies and field failures, and improve design to meet performance and quality requirements.
* Manage: We bolster our internal development team with top JDM companies to design, validate, certify and manufacture quality products, certification labs and other external consultants.
* Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale g

**Job Description:**
--------------------

Join Us in Shaping the Future

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software. As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.

The Team
  
The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs. The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.

Position Overview
  
We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on an engineering or research project that may involve compiler features, MLIR-based intermediate representations, Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), optimization, code generation, runtime or offload support, debug information, testing infrastructure, performance analysis, or developer tools. Projects may connect hardware capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Qimi. You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for a graduate student who can apply deeper technical expertise to an ambiguous engineering or research problem, evaluate alternatives, and deliver a well-supported solution or prototype.

Responsibilities
  

* Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies.
* Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase.
* Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions.
* Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project.
* Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members.
* Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team.
* Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work.

  

**Success in This Role**

* Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies.

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.

* Clear written and verbal communication.

* Ability to work independently on scoped tasks while seeking guidance when needed.

* Collaborative mindset and commitment to high-quality engineering.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical discipline.

* Graduate-level coursework, research, or project experience in compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, parallel computing, systems software, or a closely related area.

* Experience programming in C or C++ and working with complex software systems.

* Experience designing experiments, analyzing technical results, and communicating conclusions.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Familiarity with LLVM, MLIR, Clang, Flang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton, OpenMP, CUDA, or another compiler or parallel-programming ecosystem.

* Hands-on experience with LLVM or related compiler infrastructure, including front-end development, intermediate representations, optimization passes, code generation, runtimes, or debug information.

* Research or development experience involving CPU/GPU architectures, heterogeneous computing, AI/ML compilation, HPC, parallel programming, or performance optimization.

* Experience with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.

* Tile-base programming model knowledge

* Experience contributing to open-source software or working in a large collaborative codebase.

* Publications, technical reports, patents, open-source contributions, or other evidence of advanced technical work.

**Why SRC?**

With more than 400 employees, $83 million in annual revenue and nearly 80 years of RD&D experience, the Saskatchewan Research Council (SRC) is Canada’s second largest research and technology organization with 1,400 clients in 16 countries around the world. We help clients from across the world solve technology problems, make improvements, seize opportunities, maintain competitiveness, increase productivity, and develop new markets.

SRC’s Environmental Performance, Sustainability and Climate team provides environmental, technological, community engagement and management support services to the resource and industrial sectors. The team is managing a large-scale remediation project called Project CLEANS (Cleanup of Abandoned Northern Sites), which involves the remediation of 37 abandoned uranium mine and mill sites in northern Saskatchewan, with the objective of returning the sites to a state that supports safe, future use by the communities for traditional purposes. To learn more, visit www.src.sk.ca.

**Overview**

SRC’s Environmental Performance, Sustainability and Climate team is seeking an Engineering Co-op Student to engage in fieldwork activities in support of Project CLEANS. This position is a 16-month term, starting in May 2027.

**Accountabilities**

* Participate in fieldwork activities to support the assessment and remediation of abandoned uranium mines in northern Saskatchewan
* Conduct environmental sampling of soil, surface water, ground water and waste rock
* Perform radiation surveys and scanning
* Assist with environmental data management, analysis and interpretation
* Support the oversight of contractors during fieldwork
* Contribute to report preparation and the planning of field activities

**Qualifications**

* A third or fourth year environmental, geological or civil engineering student enrolled in the University of Saskatchewan Engineering Co-operative Internship Program
* Experience conducting field work is an asset

**Skills**

* Strong understanding of best practices for quality work and workplace safety
* Team player with effective interpersonal, communication, multitasking and problem-solving skills
* Willingness to learn and stay flexible as daily job tasks may vary
* Ability to self-motivate, follow detailed instructions and carry out tasks with minimal supervision
* Organizational skills and attention to detail

**Requirements**

* Valid Class 5 driver’s license
* Travel to remote, radiation-impacted abandoned mine sites in northern Saskatchewan for up to two weeks at a time during the field season (from May to October)
* Extended working hours (up to 12 hours per day) while in the field
* Out of town field trips for up to 21 days
* Traveling by small aircraft, boat and operating all-terrain vehicles
* Walking in rugged, forested terrain with 20-lb (10-kg) backpack for up to 10 hours per day
* Obtain designation as a Nuclear Energy Worker (training will be provided)

The chosen candidate will be required to provide an original Criminal Record Check that is satisfactory to SRC prior to the commencement of any employment duties. The Criminal Record Check must have been executed within the preceding 30 days of receipt.

This position is located in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan.

Deadline to apply is November 30, 2026.

Note: Applicants are also required to apply on Career Link as per the Co-op program requirements.

Please indicate on your application where you heard about the position as SRC works with several partners to support an inclusive workplace that embraces diverse backgrounds. Our goal is to engage and empower all people so they can successfully achieve their professional goals.

**As SRC strives to build a representative workforce, applications are encouraged from persons of Indigenous ancestry.**

**Hear from our Past Students**

As a working student, my internship experience at SRC has been incredibly valuable, providing me with hands-on exposure to real engineering projects and industry practices. One of the aspects I have enjoyed most is the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals and contribute to meaningful work that has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills. Throughout my placement, I have been able to apply concepts learned in my electrical engineering courses to real-world challenges while also gaining practical knowledge that cannot be learned in a classroom. This experience has increased my confidence as an engineer, and reinforced my enthusiasm for pursuing a career in engineering.

* Mustafa Emara, Electrical Engineering Co-op Student

I'm currently a Chemical Engineering student and I've worked in both the Mineral Processing and Rare Earth Elements departments. My experience at SRC as a student assistant has been incredibly valuable, from working in bench scale lab projects and pilot plants to commissioning a brand new plant. While in school, it was hard to imagine what the processing equipment even looked like, all I knew was the math behind it. Now, I can say I've actually worked with the equipment including testing it, designing procedures for it, and troubling shooting it as well. Between both departments and others I've met throughout my time at SRC I can say for certain it is a warm and welcoming work environment. Overall, my Co-Op at SRC has been a great opportunity to grow, contribute, and gain experience that I’ll carry with me throughout my career.

* Mackenzie Wallace, Chemical Engineering Co-op Student

**Job Description:**
--------------------

At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.

As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.

The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs.

The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.

You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.

* Compiler features or MLIR-based intermediate representations
* Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs)
* Optimization, code generation, runtime, or offload support
* Debug information or testing infrastructure
* Performance analysis or developer tools

Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.

new_jobs.title: Intern - Mechatronics Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Human Computer Lab is a research lab building character robots that feel alive and responsive. Our first robot, LeLamp, explores a new category of consumer robotics where everyday objects become interactive and help us reshape our attachment to technology.

Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments.

We're looking for a mechatronics intern who can move fluidly between mechanical prototyping and controls work to support LeLamp's development. You'll build and iterate on prototyping rigs, take on lower-level controls and calibration work that currently competes for our engineers' time with deeper domain work, and support mechanical design tasks as needed. As the platform matures, this role will increasingly bridge mechanical and controls — running test-rig cycles, troubleshooting integration issues, and translating mechanical design changes into controls adjustments. This is a hands-on role for someone who'd rather be a generalist across the physical stack than specialize narrowly in one domain this early in their career.

**In this role, you will:**

* Build and iterate on prototyping rigs — mechanical assembly, wiring, and basic controls integration
* Take on lower-level controls tasks (sensor wiring, calibration, simple test scripts) that free up our controls and mechanical engineers for deeper domain work
* Support mechanical design tasks as needed — CAD iteration, fixture design, fit checks
* Bridge mechanical and controls as the product matures — run reliability/test-rig cycles, troubleshoot integration issues, and translate mechanical design changes into controls adjustments
* Explore mechanistic interpretability on the models behind LeLamp’s character and behavior, using techniques like probing and activation analysis to understand why the agent responds the way it does
* Help us spot and characterize behavior we didn’t design for, especially as people interact with LeLamp in unexpected ways
* Document test results and communicate issues clearly to the team

**You may be a good fit if you:**

* Are pursuing a degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
* Have some exposure to CAD (SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion360, or similar) and basic controls/embedded work, from class projects, personal builds, or prior internships
* Have hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, machining, microcontrollers, or simple test rigs
* Have exposure to mechanistic interpretability or model-internals work (probing, activation patching, sparse autoencoders, or similar). This is a bonus, not a requirement.

* Are comfortable jumping into unfamiliar systems and can create order through chaos
* Care about users and feel ownership over outcomes, even for systems you don't own
* Think holistically about systems and approach problems with creative, outside-the-box solutions

**You will be a strong fit, if you:**

* Are a jack-of-all-trades who's drawn to hands-on prototyping over deep specialization in one domain
* Move quickly and work well in rapid iteration cycles
* Are curious about what’s actually happening inside the models we ship, not just whether the outputs look right
* Take ownership over the systems you touch, even when they're not "yours"
* Work well in small, collaborative teams, without needing much day-to-day mentorship
* Are curious, resourceful, and motivated to solve difficult problems

The early team becomes the DNA of the company. We set ourselves and others to a high standard, and we respond with kindness when things get hard but keep everyone accountable. This requires us to be curious, creative, and diverse in our thinking and approach.
  
  
We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, we encourage you to apply. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups often hold back unless they meet 100% of the criteria - we don’t want that to be the reason we miss out on great talent.

new_jobs.title: Student Project Coordinator- Buildings West
new_jobs.description:
Student Project Coordinator- Buildings WestOur internships and Co-ops are designed to provide you with a business relevant project that will allow you to independently manage your own area of responsibility, while receiving support from an assigned Supervisor and Technical Mentor. We’ll help you discover your strengths and development areas in a challenging, fun, and supportive work environment.
  
  
Projects are scoped in alignment with your term length, and typically focus on a current construction project.
  
  
We are seeking a student to join us for an 8 month co-op position starting in January 2027. This position will be based out of Richmond, BC.

**What You Will Be Working On**
===============================

Project Coordination:

* Coordinate drawings and work specific scope/trades.
* Review trade quotes, verify material quantities, hours, and rates.
* Participate in project meetings.
* Conduct deficiency walks and update deficiency logs.
* Issue warranties.
* Take and coordinate progress photos.
* Update field drawings and produce as-built drawings.

Field Coordination:

* Perform quantity takeoffs.
* Coordinate sub-trade work.
* Verify site conditions and coordinate with drawings.
* Supervise sub-trade work.
* Set up and maintain record keeping.
* Layout site lines and grades using total station.

Scheduling:

* Update project schedules.
* Create manual schedules and update schedules
* Obtain scheduling information from sub-trades.
* Create and maintain graphical scheduling
* Monitor manpower productivity.

This job description outlines the general nature and level of work performed by the Student Project Coordinator. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required for the role, and it may vary depending on assignment. Bird may modify or add to the job duties and qualifications as needed.

**Who We Need On Our Team**

  

* You are currently enrolled in Civil, Mechanical, Structural Engineering, or Construction program
* You will complete at least one more semester of education following your internship and possess a GPA of 3.0 or higher
* Ability to lead and operate within an environment where change happens frequently
* Ability to forge, grow and maintain positive relationships
* Exemplify the Ideal Team Player – Hungry, Humble, Smart
* Highly developed interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills
* Sense of urgency and strong commitment to achieving goals
* Ability to work collaboratively with a positive attitude
* Residency, or a valid work permit which would allow you to work for Bird Construction or one of our wholly owned subsidiaries
* If you are selected for a role with client specific requirements, you may be required to successfully complete a pre-employment Medical and/or Alcohol & Drug testing.
* All applications must include a current transcript

The pay range for this role is $23-$27 per hour.

**What We Are Looking For**
===========================

**For Those Who Seek to Redefine**
==================================

The greatest achievements in history are borne from the greatness within people – where human potential meets vision, and passion fuels evolution. Unlocking this potential is the most important thing we do at Bird.

As a leader in Canadian construction for over 100 years, the impact of our team is etched deeply within the core of our legacy. Beyond Bird, this impact is felt in the fundamental aspects of our everyday lives. From the critical infrastructure we depend on, to the energy and resources that keep us moving - we are powering our communities and shaping Canada’s skylines coast-to-coast-to-coast. Entrenched in the foundation of a culture built more than a century ago is an enduring quest to reimagine what is possible. Our impact is greater than ever, and we are looking for those who seek to redefine their story.

**What We Believe In**
======================

**We Put Safety First**
-----------------------

A healthy and safe work environment is non-negotiable. We build a culture of operational and psychological safety through engagement, learning and leadership.

**We Lead With Honesty**
------------------------

We speak and act with integrity, clarity and care so people can trust our word and our work. Being honest means we can deliver the best outcomes and consistent results.

**We Are Stronger Together**
----------------------------

Success is a team effort. Our inclusive workplace enables our combined expertise, humility and creativity to unlock our greater potential.

**We Are Driven To Do Great Work**
----------------------------------

We built our name on quality. We have a passion for excellence in our work and relationships that honours our businesses and our industry.

**We Create Opportunity**
-------------------------

Rooted in a solid foundation, we adapt and grow to face the future. We are committed to elevating each other to chart the best path forward in an evolving world.

At Bird, we value Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) and believe it is essential to our success. We will continue to listen, learn, and take action in our commitment to building progress in our organization, and the industry as a whole. Cultivating an environment where all employees feel included, seen, and have a sense of belonging is core to Bird’s culture. We commit to proactively employing a workforce that reflects the communities in which we work, fostering an environment of continuous learning, and never compromising on our values.

new_jobs.title: Software Developer Intern
new_jobs.description:
**Your TAIT Internship**
========================

At TAIT, interns do more than observe - they contribute. Our immersive internship program connects your interests and area of study with meaningful, hands-on work alongside teams that push the boundaries of what is possible.

You will help bring real projects to life, learn from industry experts, and build skills that move your career forward. We provide mentorship and support while empowering you to set goals, take initiative, and shape your experience.

Ready to challenge yourself, share new ideas, and make an impact? Your journey starts here.

**What You Need to Know**
=========================

* Location: Montreal, QC
* Duration: May 17, 2027 - August 13, 2027
* Compensation: $29.00 CAD per hour
* Schedule: 40 hours per week on first shift, based on project and business needs
* Eligibility: Applicants must meet the work authorization requirements for the country where the role is based

**Your Role at TAIT**
=====================

As a Software Development Intern, you will work alongside experienced developers to learn how a software team designs, builds, tests, and maintains its products. You will contribute to clearly defined tasks matched to your experience, with opportunities to take on more complex work as your skills and confidence grow.

**What You Will Work On**
=========================

* Complete clearly defined development tasks, such as straightforward features, bug fixes, tests, and documentation improvements.
* Write clear, maintainable code using established team standards and practices.
* Build familiarity with the team's technologies, tools, codebase, and development workflow.
* Assist with testing and troubleshooting by identifying, investigating, and communicating software issues.
* Participate in code reviews, pairing sessions, and team discussions, applying feedback to improve your work.
* Document assigned work, communicate progress and challenges, and ask questions when support is needed.
* Work with your mentor to set learning goals and reflect on your progress throughout the internship.

**What You Bring**
==================

To qualify for this internship, you should have:

* Current enrollment in a degree, DEC, DEP, or other relevant program in Computer Science, Software Development, or a related discipline, or equivalent foundational learning.
* An expected graduation date between December 2026 and May 2028.
* A GPA of 3.0 or above, or equivalent academic standing where applicable.
* A basic understanding of programming concepts, including variables, control flow, functions, and data structures.
* Interest in learning development tools and practices such as version control, testing, and code review.
* A thoughtful approach to problem-solving, attention to detail, and willingness to work through unfamiliar tasks with support.
* Clear communication skills, a collaborative mindset, curiosity, and openness to feedback.

**Where This Could Take You**
=============================

* Software Developer or Software Engineer
* Quality Assurance or Test Automation Engineer
* DevOps or Platform Engineer

**Why Intern at TAIT**
======================

* Meaningful Work: Contribute to projects that matter, including experiences seen by millions of people.
* Professional Growth: Gain practical experience and develop skills that support your future career.
* Mentorship: Learn from experienced professionals who provide guidance, feedback, and support.
* Innovation: Collaborate with creative teams developing forward-thinking solutions.
* Connections: Build relationships with industry leaders, experienced colleagues, and fellow interns.
* Future Opportunities: Successful interns may be considered for full-time or part-time roles.

Bring your ideas to life, grow your skills, and help us create moments that move people. Apply today and start your journey with TAIT.
